cyclamen: Any of various flowering plants, of the genus Cyclamen, widely cultivated as a houseplant, having decorative leaves and solitary flowers.
cycle: An interval of space or time in which one set of events or phenomena is completed.
cyclone: (broad sense) A weather phenomenon consisting of a system of winds rotating around a center of low atmospheric pressure
cylinder: A surface created by projecting a closed two-dimensional curve along an axis intersecting the plane of the curve.
cymbal: A concave plate of brass or bronze that produces a sharp, ringing sound when struck: played either in pairs, by striking them together, or singly by striking with a drumstick or the like.
cynic: A person who believes that all people are motivated by selfishness.
cyst: A pouch or sac without opening, usually membranous and containing morbid matter, which develops in one of the natural cavities or in the substance of an organ.
cytokine: Any of various small regulatory proteins that regulate the cells of the immune system.
cytoplasm: The contents of a cell except for the nucleus. It includes cytosol, organelles, vesicles, and the cytoskeleton.
daffodil: A bulbous plant of the genus Narcissus, with yellow flowers and a trumpet shaped corona, especially Narcissus pseudonarcissus, the national flower of Wales.
dagger: A stabbing weapon, similar to a sword but with a short, double-edged blade.
dahlia: Any plant of the genus Dahlia, tuberous perennial flowering plants native to Mexico.
daikon: An East Asian cultivar or subspecies of radish (Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus, syn. Raphanus sativus) bearing a large, white, carrot-shaped taproot consumed throughout East and South Asia but grown in North America primarily as a fallow crop for its fast-growing leaves (used as animal fodder) and as a soil ripper.
daily: Something that is produced, consumed, used, or done every day.
dairy: (also dairy products or dairy produce) Products produced from milk.
daisy: A wild flowering plant Bellis perennis of the Asteraceae family, with a yellow head and white petals
dam: A structure placed across a flowing body of water to stop the flow or part of the flow, generally for purposes such as retaining or diverting some of the water or retarding the release of accumulated water to avoid abrupt flooding.
damage: Injury or harm; the condition or measure of something not being intact.
dame: Usually capitalized as Dame: a title equivalent to Sir for a female knight.
damn: The use of "damn" as a curse.
dance: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
dancer: A person who dances, usually as a job or profession.
dancing: To move with rhythmic steps or movements, especially in time to music.
dandelion: Any of the several species of plant in the genus Taraxacum, characterised by yellow flower heads and notched, broad-ended leaves, especially the common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale).
dark: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.
darkness: The state of being dark; lack of light.
dart: A pointed missile weapon, intended to be thrown by the hand, for example a short lance or javelin
dash: Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar).
dashboard: A panel under the windscreen of a motor car or aircraft, containing indicator dials, compartments, and sometimes controls.
data: (plural: data) A measurement of something on a scale understood by both the recorder (a person or device) and the reader (another person or device). The scale is arbitrarily defined, such as from 1 to 10 by ones, 1 to 100 by 0.1, or simply true or false, on or off, yes, no, or maybe, etc.
database: (general) A collection of (usually) organized information in a regular structure, usually but not necessarily in a machine-readable format accessible by a computer.
date: The fruit of the date palm, Phoenix dactylifera, somewhat in the shape of an olive, containing a soft, sweet pulp and enclosing a hard kernel.
dawn: The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise.
daybed: A couch that can be used as a sofa by day and a bed by night.
daylight: The light from the Sun, as opposed to that from any other source.
dead: (with "the", a demonstrative, or a possessive) Those who have died.
deadline: A time limit in the form of a date on or before which something must be completed.
deal: A division, a portion, a share.
dealer: One who deals in goods, especially automobiles; a middleman.
dealing: To distribute among a number of recipients, to give out as one’s portion or share.
death: The cessation of life and all associated processes; the end of an organism's existence as an entity independent from its environment and its return to an inert, nonliving state.
deathwatch: A vigil beside a dying person
debate: An argument, or discussion, usually in an ordered or formal setting, often with more than two people, generally ending with a vote or other decision.
debris: Rubble, wreckage, scattered remains of something destroyed.
debt: An action, state of mind, or object one has an obligation to perform for another, adopt toward another, or give to another.
debtor: A person or firm that owes money; one in debt; one who owes a debt
decade: A group, set, or series of ten , particularly:
decadence: A state of moral or artistic decline or deterioration; decay
decency: The quality of being decent; propriety.
decimal: A number expressed in the base-ten system, a fractional numeral written in this system.
decision-making: The process of reaching a decision.
deck: Any raised flat surface that can be walked on: a balcony; a porch; a raised patio; a flat rooftop.
declaration: A written or oral indication of a fact, opinion, or belief.
declination: At a given point, the angle between magnetic north and true north.
decoder: A person who decodes secret messages
decongestant: A drug that relieves congestion, e.g. pseudoephedrine.
decoration: The act of adorning, embellishing, or honoring; ornamentation.
decrease: An amount by which a quantity is decreased.
dedication: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated.
deduce: To reach a conclusion by applying rules of logic to given premises.
deduction: That which is deducted; that which is subtracted or removed
deed: An action or act; something that is done.
deep: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.
deer: A ruminant mammal with antlers and hooves of the family Cervidae, or one of several similar animals from related families of the order Artiodactyla
default: The condition of failing to meet an obligation.
defeat: To overcome in battle or contest.
defendant: Serving, or suitable, for defense; defensive, defending.
defender: Someone who defends people or property
defense: The action of defending or protecting from attack, danger, or injury.
deficit: Deficiency in amount or quality; a falling short; lack.
definition: A statement of the meaning of a word or word group or a sign or symbol (dictionary definitions).
deformation: The act of deforming, or state of being deformed.
degradation: The act of reducing in rank, character, or reputation, or of abasing; a lowering from one's standing or rank in office or society
degree: A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university or, in some countries, a college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.)
delay: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.
deliberation: The act of deliberating, or of weighing and examining the reasons for and against a choice or measure; careful consideration; mature reflection.
demand: The desire to purchase goods and services.
democracy: Rule by the people, especially as a form of government; either directly or through elected representatives (representative democracy).
democrat: A supporter of democracy; an advocate of democratic politics (originally as opposed to the aristocrats in Revolutionary France).
demur: Stop; pause; hesitation as to proceeding; suspense of decision or action; scruple.
den: A small cavern or hollow place in the side of a hill, or among rocks; especially, a cave used by a wild animal for shelter or concealment.
denim: A textile often made of cotton with a distinct diagonal pattern.
denominator: The number or expression written below the line in a fraction (such as 2 in ½).
density: A measure of the mass of matter contained by a unit volume.
dentist: A medical doctor who specializes in dentistry.
deodorant: Any agent acting to eliminate, reduce, mask, or control odor.
departure: The act of departing or something that has departed.
dependency: A state of dependence; a refusal to exercise initiative.
dependent: One who relies on another for support
deployment: An arrangement or classification of things.
deposit: Sediment or rock that is not native to its present location or is different from the surrounding material. Sometimes refers to ore or gems.
deposition: The removal of someone from office.
depot: A storage facility, in particular, a warehouse.
depression: In psychotherapy and psychiatry, a state of mind producing serious, long-term lowering of enjoyment of life or inability to visualize a happy future.
depth: The vertical distance below a surface; the degree to which something is deep
deputy: One appointed as the substitute of another, and empowered to act for them, in their name or their behalf; a substitute in office
derby: Any of several annual horse races.
derivation: A leading or drawing off of water from a stream or source.
derrick: A device that is used for lifting and moving large objects.
descendant: One who is the progeny of a specified person, at any distance of time or through any number of generations.
descent: An instance of descending; act of coming down.
description: A sketch or account of anything in words; a portraiture or representation in language; an enumeration of the essential qualities of a thing or species.
desert: (usually in the plural) That which is deserved or merited; a just punishment or reward
design: A specification of an object or process, referring to requirements to be satisfied and thus conditions to be met for them to solve a problem.
designation: The act of designating; a pointing out or showing; indication.
designer: A person who designs something, or who designs things as a profession.
desk: A table, frame, or case, in past centuries usually with a sloping top but now usually with a flat top, for the use of writers and readers. It often has a drawer or repository underneath.
desktop: The top surface of a desk.
dessert: A sweet confection served as the last course of a meal
destination: The act of destining or appointing.
destiny: That to which any person or thing is destined; a predetermined state; a condition predestined by the Divine or by human will
detail: Something small enough to escape casual notice.
detainee: Someone who is detained, especially in custody or confinement.
detection: The act of detecting or sensing something; discovering something that was hidden or disguised.
detective: (law enforcement) A police officer who looks for evidence as part of solving a crime; an investigator.
detector: A device capable of registering a specific substance or physical phenomenon, and that optionally sounds an alarm or triggers a warning.
detention: The act of detaining or the state of being detained.
determination: The act of determining, or the state of being determined.
detour: A diversion or deviation from one's original route.
devastation: The act of devastating, or the state of being devastated; a laying waste.
developer: A person or entity engaged in the creation or improvement of certain classes of products.
developing: To change with a specific direction, progress.
development: The process of developing; growth, directed change.
deviance: Actions or behaviors that violate formal and informal cultural norms such as laws and customs.
deviation: The act of deviating; wandering off the correct or true path or road
device: Any piece of equipment made for a particular purpose, especially a mechanical or electrical one.
dew: Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
dhow: A traditional sailing vessel used along the coasts of Arabia, East Africa, and the Indian Ocean, generally having a single mast and a lateen sail.
diabetes: Diabetes insipidus; any condition characterized by excessive or incontinent urine, now specifically as caused by impaired production of, or response to, the antidiuretic hormone vasopressin.
diadem: An ornamental headband worn as a badge of royalty.
diagnosis: To determine which disease is causing a sick person's signs and symptoms; to find the diagnosis.
diagram: A plan, drawing, sketch or outline to show how something works, or show the relationships between the parts of a whole.
dial: A graduated, circular scale over which a needle moves to show a measurement (such as speed).
dialect: A variety of a language that is characteristic of a particular area, community or social group, differing from other varieties of the same language in relatively minor ways as regards grammar, phonology, and lexicon.
dialogue: A conversation or other form of discourse between two or more individuals.
diamond: A glimmering glass-like mineral that is an allotrope of carbon in which each atom is surrounded by four others in the form of a tetrahedron.
diaper: A textile fabric having a diamond-shaped pattern formed by alternating directions of thread.
diaphragm: In mammals, a sheet of muscle separating the thorax from the abdomen, contracted and relaxed in respiration to draw air into and expel air from the lungs; also called thoracic diaphragm.
diary: A daily log of experiences, especially those of the writer.
dibble: A pointed implement used to make holes in the ground in which to set out plants or to plant seeds.
dictator: A totalitarian leader of a country, nation, or government.
diction: Choice and use of words, especially with regard to effective communication.
dictionary: A reference work with a list of words from one or more languages, normally ordered alphabetically, explaining each word's meaning, and sometimes containing information on its etymology, pronunciation, usage, translations, and other data.
die: To stop living; to become dead; to undergo death.
diesel: A fuel derived from petroleum (or other oils) but heavier than gasoline/petrol. Used to power diesel engines which burn this fuel using the heat produced when air is compressed.
diet: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
differential: The differential gear in an automobile etc
difficulty: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
diffuse: To spread over or through as in air, water, or other matter, especially by fluid motion or passive means.
dig: An archeological or paleontological investigation, or the site where such an investigation is taking place.
digestion: The process, in the gastrointestinal tract, by which food is converted into substances that can be utilized by the body.
digger: A large piece of machinery that digs holes or trenches; an excavator.
digging: To move hard-packed earth out of the way, especially downward to make a hole with a shovel. Or to drill, or the like, through rocks, roads, or the like. More generally, to make any similar hole by moving material out of the way.
digit: A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university or, in some countries, a college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.)
dignity: The state of being dignified or worthy of esteem: elevation of mind or character.
dilapidation: The state of being dilapidated, reduced to decay, partially ruined.
dill: Anethum graveolens (the type species of the genus Anethum), a herb, the seeds of which are moderately warming, pungent, and aromatic, formerly used as a soothing medicine for children; also known as dillseed.
dilution: The process of making something dilute.
dime: A coin worth one-tenth of a U.S. dollar.
dimension: A single aspect of a given thing.
dimple: A small depression or indentation in a surface.
dinghy: A small open boat, propelled by oars or paddles, carried as a tender, lifeboat, or pleasure craft on a ship.
dining: To eat; to eat dinner or supper.
dinner: A midday meal (in a context in which the evening meal is called supper or tea).
dinosaur: In scientific usage, any of the animals belonging to the clade Dinosauria, especially those that existed during the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods and are now extinct.
dioxide: Any oxide containing two oxygen atoms in each molecule.
dip: A lower section of a road or geological feature.
diploma: A document issued by an educational institution testifying that the recipient has earned a degree or has successfully completed a particular course of study.
diplomacy: The art and practice of conducting international relations by negotiating alliances, treaties, agreements etc., bilaterally or multilaterally, between states and sometimes international organizations, or even between polities with varying status, such as those of monarchs and their princely vassals.
dipstick: A stick or rod used to measure the depth of a liquid. Often used to check the level at which a liquid in an opaque or inaccessible tank or reservoir stands; gauge.
direction: A theoretical line (physically or mentally) followed from a point of origin or towards a destination. May be relative (e.g. up, left, outbound, dorsal), geographical (e.g. north), rotational (e.g. clockwise), or with respect to an object or location (e.g. toward Boston).
directive: An instruction or guideline that indicates how to perform an action or reach a goal.
director: One who directs; the person in charge of managing a department or directorate (e.g., director of engineering), project, or production (as in a show or film, e.g., film director).
directory: A list of names, addresses etc, of specific classes of people or organizations, often in alphabetical order or in some classification.
dirndl: A traditional Alpine women's dress having a tight bodice and full skirt
disability: State of being disabled; deprivation or want of ability; absence of competent physical, intellectual, or moral power, means, fitness, and the like.
disadvantage: A weakness or undesirable characteristic; a con.
disappointment: A feeling of sadness or frustration when a strongly held expectation is not met.
disarmament: The reduction or the abolition of the military forces and armaments of a nation, and of its capability to wage war.
disaster: An unexpected natural or man-made catastrophe of substantial extent causing significant physical damage or destruction, loss of life or sometimes permanent change to the natural environment.
discharge: Pus or exudate (other than blood) from a wound or orifice, usually due to infection or pathology.
disclaimer: One who disclaims, disowns, or renounces.
disco: A genre of dance music that was popular in the 1970s, characterized by elements of soul music with a strong Latin-American beat and often accompanied by pulsating lights.
discrepancy: An inconsistency between facts or sentiments.
discretion: The quality of being discreet or circumspect.
discrimination: Discernment, the act of discriminating, discerning, distinguishing, noting or perceiving differences between things, with intent to understand rightly and make correct decisions.
discussion: Conversation or debate concerning a particular topic.
disdain: A feeling of contempt or scorn.
disease: An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired.
disengagement: Release or detachment from a physical situation or other involvement.
disguise: Material (such as clothing, makeup, a wig) used to alter one’s visual appearance in order to hide one's identity or assume another.
disgust: An intense dislike or loathing someone feels for something bad or nasty.
dish: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
disk: A thin, flat, circular plate or similar object.
disparity: The state of being unequal; difference.
dispatch: A message sent quickly, as a shipment, a prompt settlement of a business, or an important official message sent by a diplomat, or military officer.
displacement: The act of displacing, or the state of being displaced; a putting out of place.
disposal: An arrangement, categorization or classification of things.
disposition: The arrangement or placement of certain things.
dispute: An argument or disagreement, a failure to agree.
disregard: The act or state of deliberately not paying attention or caring about; misregard.
disruption: An interruption to the regular flow or sequence of something.
dissemination: The act of disseminating, or the state of being disseminated; diffusion for propagation and permanence; a scattering or spreading abroad, as of ideas, beliefs, etc.
dissonance: A harsh, discordant combination of sounds.
distance: The amount of space between two points, usually geographical points, usually (but not necessarily) measured along a straight line.
distinction: That which distinguishes; a single occurrence of a determining factor or feature, the fact of being divided; separation, discrimination.
distribution: An act of distributing or state of being distributed.
distributor: One who or that which distributes.
district: An administrative division of an area.
divan: A Muslim council of state, specifically that of viziers of the Ottoman Empire that discussed and recommended new laws and law changes to a higher authority (the sultan).
diver: Someone who dives, especially as a sport.
diversity: The quality of being diverse or different; difference or unlikeness.
dividend: A number or expression that is to be divided by another.
divine: One skilled in divinity; a theologian.
division: The act or process of dividing anything.
divorce: The legal dissolution of a marriage.
dock: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially common dock, and used as potherbs and in folk medicine, especially in curing nettle rash.
doctor: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are D.O., DPM, M.D., DMD, DDS, in the US or MBBS in the UK.
doctorate: The highest degree awarded by a university faculty.
doctrine: A belief or tenet, especially about philosophical or theological matters.
document: An original or official paper used as the basis, proof, or support of anything else, including any writing, book, or other instrument conveying information pertinent to such proof or support.
documentary: A film, TV program, publication etc. which presents a social, political, scientific or historical subject in a factual or informative manner.
documentation: Something transposed from a thought to a document; the written account of an idea.
doe: A female deer; also used of similar animals such as antelope, (less commonly goat as nanny is also used).
dog: A mammal, Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, that has been domesticated for thousands of years, of highly variable appearance due to human breeding.
doggie: A dog, especially a small one.
dogsled: A sled, pulled by dogs over ice and snow.
dogwood: Any of various small trees of the genus Cornus, especially the wild cornel and the flowering cornel
doll: A toy in the form of a human.
dollar: Official designation for currency in some parts of the world, including Canada, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, and elsewhere. Its symbol is $.
dollop: A considerable lump, scoop, or quantity of something, especially soft food.
dolman: A long, loose garment with narrow sleeves and an opening in the front, generally worn by Turks.
dolphin: A carnivorous aquatic mammal in one of several families of order Cetacea, famed for its intelligence and occasional willingness to approach humans.
domain: A geographic area owned or controlled by a single person or organization.
dome: A structural element resembling the hollow upper half of a sphere; a cupola
donation: A voluntary gift or contribution for a specific cause.
donkey: A domestic animal, Equus asinus asinus, similar to a horse
donut: A deep-fried piece of dough or batter, commonly made in a toroidal or ellipsoidal shape, and mixed with various sweeteners and flavors, sometimes filled with jelly, custard or cream.
door: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. Doors are frequently made of wood or metal. May have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold the door closed and a lock that ensures the door cannot be opened without the key.
doorbell: A device on or adjacent to an outer door for announcing one's presence. It can be mechanical, directly sounding a bell, or a button that electrically sounds a chime or buzzer inside the building.
doorknob: A circular device attached to a door, the rotation of which permits the unlatching of the door.
doorway: The passage of a door; a door-shaped entrance into a house or a room.
dory: A small flat-bottomed boat with pointed or somewhat pointed ends, used for fishing both offshore and on rivers.
double: Twice the number, amount, size, etc.
doubt: Disbelief or uncertainty (about something); a particular instance of such disbelief or uncertainty.
dough: A thick, malleable substance made by mixing flour with other ingredients such as water, eggs, and/or butter, that is made into a particular form and then baked.
doughnut: A deep-fried piece of dough or batter, commonly of a toroidal (a ring doughnut) shape, often mixed with various sweeteners and flavourings; or flattened sphere (a filled doughnut) shape filled with jam, custard or cream.
downfall: A precipitous decline in fortune; death or rapid deterioration, as in status or wealth.
downforce: Any force (produced by aerodynamics or gravity etc) that acts downwards
downgrade: A reduction of a rating, as a financial or credit rating.
download: A file transfer to the local computer.
downstairs: The lower floor of a house, at ground level.
downtown: The main business part of a city or town, usually located at or near its center.
downturn: A downward trend, or the beginnings of one; a decline.
draft: A current of air, usually coming into a room or vehicle.
drag: Resistance of the air (or some other fluid) to something moving through it.
dragon: A legendary serpentine or reptilian creature.
dragonfly: An insect of the suborder Epiprocta or, more strictly, the infraorder Anisoptera, having four long transparent wings held perpendicular to a long body when perched.
dragster: A heavily modified or custom-built vehicle used in drag racing.
drain: A conduit allowing liquid to flow out of an otherwise contained volume; a plughole (UK)
drainage: A natural or artificial removal of fluid from a given area by its draining away.
drama: A composition, normally in prose, telling a story and intended to be represented by actors impersonating the characters and speaking the dialogue
dramaturge: Someone who writes or adapts theater plays, a playwright, dramatist, especially one connected with a specific theater or company.
draw: The result of a contest that neither side has won; a tie.
drawbridge: A hinged bridge which can be raised (to prevent its being crossed, as across a moat, or to allow watercraft to travel beneath it).
drawer: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
dream: Imaginary events seen in the mind while sleeping.
dredger: A vessel equipped for the removal of sand or sediment from the seabed.
dress: An item of clothing (usually worn by a woman or young girl) which both covers the upper part of the body and includes skirts below the waist.
dresser: An item of kitchen furniture, like a cabinet with shelves, for storing crockery or utensils.
dressing: Material applied to a wound for protection or therapy.
drill: A tool used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
drink: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.
drinking: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.
drive: Motivation to do or achieve something; ability coupled with ambition.
driver: One who drives something, in any sense of the verb to drive.
driveway: Short private road that leads to a house or garage.
driving: To provide an impetus for motion or other physical change, to move an object by means of the provision of force thereto.
drop: A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape via surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid.
drug: A substance used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.
drum: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone.
drunk: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.
dryer: One who, or that which, dries; a desiccative.
duck: To quickly lower the head or body in order to prevent it from being struck by something.
dud: A device or machine that is useless because it does not work properly or has failed to work, such as a bomb, or explosive projectile.
dude: A man, generally a younger man.
duel: Arranged, regular combat between two private persons, often over a matter of honor.
duffel: A kind of coarse woolen cloth, having a thick nap or frieze.
dugout: A canoe made from a hollowed-out log.
dulcimer: A stringed instrument, with strings stretched across a sounding board, usually trapezoidal. It is played on the lap or horizontally on a table. Some have their own legs. These musical instruments are played by plucking on the strings (traditionally with a quill) or by tapping on them (in the case of the hammer dulcimers).
dumbwaiter: A small elevator used to move food etc. from one floor of a building to another.
dump: A place where waste or garbage is left; a ground or place for dumping ashes, refuse, etc.; a disposal site.
dump truck: A heavy truck, for carrying loose, bulk cargo, having a hinged bed that allows the contents to be unloaded onto the ground
dune: A ridge or hill of sand piled up by the wind.
dune buggy: A recreational vehicle with large tires, designed for use on beaches and sand dunes.
dungarees: Heavy denim pants or trousers, usually with bib and braces, worn especially as work clothing.
dungeon: An underground prison or vault, typically built underneath a castle.
duration: An amount of time or a particular time interval.
durian: Any of several trees, genus Durio, of Southeast Asia.
dusk: A period of time at the end of day when the sun is below the horizon but before the full onset of night, especially the darker part of twilight.
dust storm: Phenomenon in which gale- to hurricane-force winds blow particles up in a planet's atmosphere.
duster: An object, now especially a cloth, used for dusting surfaces etc.
duty: That which one is morally or legally obligated to do.
dwarf: Any member of a race of beings from (especially Scandinavian and other Germanic) folklore, usually depicted as having some sort of supernatural powers and being skilled in crafting and metalworking, often as short with long beards, and sometimes as clashing with elves.
dwell: A period of time in which a system or component remains in a given state.
dwelling: A house or place in which a person lives; a habitation, a home.
dynamics: The branch of mechanics that is concerned with the effects of forces on the motion of objects.
dynamite: A class of explosives made from nitroglycerine in an absorbent medium such as kieselguhr, used in mining and blasting; invented by Alfred Nobel in 1867.
dynamo: An electricity generator, a dynamo-electric machine.
dynasty: A series of rulers or dynasts from one family.
dysfunction: A failure to function in an expected or complete manner. Usually refers to a disorder in a bodily organ (e.g. erectile dysfunction), a mental disorder, or the improper behavior of a social group.
e-mail: A system for transferring messages from one computer to another, usually through a network.
e-reader: A hardware device used to read e-books.
eagle: Any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.
eaglet: The immature young of an eagle; an eagle chick.
ear: The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.
eardrum: A thin membrane that separates the outer ear from the middle ear and transmits sound from the air to the malleus.
earmuffs: Objects designed to cover a person's ears for protection against cold or noise. They consist of a thermoplastic or metal head-band, that fits over the top of the head, and a pad at each end, to cover the external ears.
earplug: A piece of protective gear meant to be inserted in the ear canal to protect the wearer's hearing from loud noises or the intrusion of water.
earring: A piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
earrings: A piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
earth: The third planet of the Solar System; the world upon which humans live.

fog: A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
folder: An organizer that papers are kept in, usually with an index tab, to be stored as a single unit in a filing cabinet.
folk: A grouping of smaller peoples or tribes as a nation.
folklore: The tales, legends and superstitions of a particular ethnic population.
follower: One who follows, comes after another.
following: To go after; to pursue; to move behind in the same path or direction.
fondue: A dish made of melted cheese, chocolate etc., or of a boiling liquid into which food can be dipped.
font: A receptacle in a church for holy water, especially one used in baptism.

foodstuffs: A material that may be used as food.
fool: A person with poor judgment or little intelligence.

footage: An amount of film or tape that has been used to record something.
football: (general) A sport played on foot in which teams attempt to get a ball into a goal or zone defended by the other team.
footnote: A short piece of text, often numbered, placed at the bottom of a printed page, that adds a comment, citation, reference etc, to a designated part of the main text.
footprint: The impression of the foot in a soft substance such as sand or snow.
footrest: A support on which to rest the feet.
footstep: The mark or impression left by a foot; a track.
footstool: A low stool for supporting the feet while seated.
footwear: Items or an item of clothing that is worn on the foot; a shoe, sandal, etc.
forage: Fodder for animals, especially cattle and horses.
forager: An animal or person who forages
foray: A sudden or irregular incursion in border warfare; hence, any irregular incursion for war or spoils; a raid.
force: Strength or energy of body or mind; active power; vigour; might; capacity of exercising an influence or producing an effect.
ford: A location where a stream is shallow and the bottom has good footing, making it possible to cross from one side to the other with no bridge, by walking, riding, or driving through the water; a crossing.
forearm: The part of the arm between the wrist and the elbow.
forebear: To keep away from; to avoid; to abstain from.
forecast: An estimation of a future condition.
forehead: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
foreigner: A person from a foreign country.
forelimb: The anterior limb (or equivalent appendage) of an animal
forest: A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.
forestry: The science of planting and growing trees in forests.
forgery: The act of forging metal into shape.
fork: A pronged tool having a long straight handle, used for digging, lifting, throwing etc.

format: The layout of a publication or document.
formicarium: A vivarium used for the study of ants and ant colonies.
fort: A fortified defensive structure stationed with troops.
fortress: A fortified place; a large and permanent fortification, sometimes including a town; for example a fort, a castle; a stronghold; a place of defense or security.
foundation: The act of founding, fixing, establishing, or beginning to erect.
founder: One who founds or establishes (especially said of a company, project, organisation, state)
fountain: A natural source of water; a spring.
fourths: (not used in the plural) The person or thing in the fourth position.
fox: A red fox, small carnivore (Vulpes vulpes), related to dogs and wolves, with red or silver fur and a bushy tail.
foxglove: Digitalis, a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous biennials native to the Old World, certain of which are prized for their showy flowers. The drug digitalis or digoxin was first isolated from the plant.
fraction: A part of a whole, especially a comparatively small part.
frame: The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
framework: A support structure comprising joined parts or conglomerated particles and intervening open spaces of similar or larger size.
fratricide: The killing of one's brother (or sister).
fraud: The crime of stealing or otherwise illegally obtaining money by use of deception tactics.
fraudster: A person who practices fraud; a swindler.
freckle: A small brownish or reddish pigmentation spot on the surface of the skin.
freedom: The state of being free, of not being imprisoned or enslaved.
freelance: Someone who sells their services to clients without a long-term employment contract.
freezer: An appliance or room used to store food or other perishable items at temperatures below 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit).
freezing: Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature.
freighter: One who loads a ship, or one who charters and loads a ship.
frenzy: A state of wild activity or panic.
freon: Any of several non-flammable refrigerants based on halogenated hydrocarbon including R-12, R-22, and R-23.
frequency: The rate of occurrence of anything; the relationship between incidence and time period.
fresco: A cool, refreshing state of the air; coolness, duskiness, shade.
friction: The rubbing of one object or surface against another.
friend: A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.
fries: (usually in the plural, fries) A fried strip of potato.
frigate: An obsolete type of sailing warship with a single continuous gun deck, typically used for patrolling, blockading, etc, but not in line of battle.
fright: A state of terror excited by the sudden appearance of danger; sudden and violent fear, usually of short duration; a sudden alarm.
fritter: A dish made by deep-frying food coated in batter.
frock: A dress, a piece of clothing for a female, which consists of a skirt and a cover for the upper body.
frog: A small tailless amphibian of the order Anura that typically hops.
front: The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves.
frontier: The part of a country which borders or faces another country or unsettled region
frost: A cover of minute ice crystals on objects that are exposed to the air. Frost is formed by the same process as dew, except that the temperature of the frosted object is below freezing.
frown: A facial expression in which the eyebrows are brought together, and the forehead is wrinkled, usually indicating displeasure, sadness or worry, or less often confusion or concentration.
fruit: (often in the plural) In general, a product of plant growth useful to man or animals.
frustration: The feeling of annoyance when one's actions are criticized or hindered
fry: (usually in the plural, fries) A fried strip of potato.
fuel: Substance consumed to provide energy through combustion, or through chemical or nuclear reaction.
fugato: A fugal passage in a composition that is not a strict or complete fugue.
full: Containing the maximum possible amount that can fit in the space available.
function: What something does or is used for.
functionality: The ability to perform a task or function; that set of functions that something is able or equipped to perform.
fund: A sum or source of money.

funeral: A ceremony to honour and remember a deceased person. Often distinguished from a memorial service by the presence of the body of the deceased.
fur: The hairy coat of various mammal species, especially when fine, soft and thick.
furnace: An industrial heating device, e.g. for smelting metal or baking ceramics.
furniture: Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
furry: An animal character with human-like characteristics; most commonly refers to such characters created by members of the furry subculture.
fusarium: Any of various fungi, of the genus Fusarium, some of which are pathogenic to plants and animals.
futon: A thin mattress of tufted cotton or similar material, placed on a floor or on a raised, foldable frame as a bed.
future: The time ahead; those moments yet to be experienced.
gadget: A thing whose name cannot be remembered; thingamajig, doohickey.
gaffe: A foolish and embarrassing error, especially one made in public.
gaffer: A chief lighting technician for a motion-picture or television production.
gaiters: A covering of cloth or leather for the ankle and instep.
gallery: An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of works of art.

gallon: A unit of volume, equivalent to eight pints
galoshes: A waterproof overshoe used to provide protection from rain or snow.
gambling: To take a risk, with the potential of a positive outcome.
gamebird: Any kind of bird hunted for food or sport.
gap: An opening in anything made by breaking or parting.
garage: A building (or section of a building) used to store a car or cars, tools and other miscellaneous items.
garb: Fashion, style of dressing oneself up.
garbage: Food waste material of any kind.
garden: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.

gazebo: A belvedere, either a type of summer-house or a roofed, detached porch-like structure, usually in a yard, park or lawn.
gazelle: An antelope of either of the genera Gazella (mostly native to Africa) or Procapra (native to Asia), capable of running at high speeds for long periods.
gear: Equipment or paraphernalia, especially that used for an athletic endeavor.
gearshift: That part of a gearbox involved in changing gear, including the gear lever and the forks attached to it.

general: A general fact or proposition; a generality.
generation: The fact of creating something, or bringing something into being; production, creation.
generator: One who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces.

genetics: The branch of biology that deals with the transmission and variation of inherited characteristics, in particular chromosomes and DNA.
genie: A jinn, a being descended from the jann, normally invisible to the human eye, but who may also appear in animal or human form.
genius: Someone possessing extraordinary intelligence or skill; especially somebody who has demonstrated this by a creative or original work in science, music, art etc.

genre: A kind; a stylistic category or sort, especially of literature or other artworks.

geography: A description of the earth: a treatise or textbook on geography; an atlas or gazetteer.

ghost: The spirit; the soul of man.

gift: Something given to another voluntarily, without charge.

girdle: That which girds, encircles, or encloses; a circumference
girl: A female child, adolescent, or a young woman.
girlfriend: A female partner in an unmarried romantic relationship.
git: A silly, incompetent, stupid, annoying or childish person (usually a man).
glacier: A large body of ice which flows under its own mass, usually downhill.
gladiolus: The center part of the sternum.
gland: An organ that synthesizes a substance, such as hormones or breast milk, and releases it, often into the bloodstream (endocrine gland) or into cavities inside the body or its outer surface (exocrine gland).
glee: Joy; happiness great delight, especially from one's own good fortune or from another's misfortune.
glen: A secluded and narrow valley, especially one with a river running through it; a dale; a depression between hills.

glimpse: A brief look, glance, or peek.

glue: A hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive; or any sticky adhesive substance.

goal: A result that one is attempting to achieve.

god: A being such as a monotheistic God: a single divine creator and ruler of the universe.

godparent: The person who stood for a child during a naming ceremony or baptism
goggles: Protective eyewear set in a flexible frame to fit snugly against the face.
gold: A heavy yellow elemental metal of great value, with atomic number 79 and symbol Au.
goldfish: A type of small fish, Carassius auratus, typically orange-colored.
golf: A ball game played by individuals competing against one another in which the object is to hit a ball into each of a series of (usually 18 or nine) holes in the minimum number of strokes.

gong: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal disk that emits a sonorous sound when struck with a soft hammer.
good-bye: An utterance of goodbye, the wishing of farewell to someone.
goodbye: An utterance of goodbye, the wishing of farewell to someone.
goodie: A good character in a story, often a hero.
goodness: The state or characteristic of being good.
goodwill: A favorably disposed attitude toward someone or something.
goose: Any of various grazing waterfowl of the family Anatidae, which have feathers and webbed feet and are capable of flying, swimming, and walking on land, and which are bigger than ducks.

gorilla: The largest of the apes, native to the forests of central Africa, and known for their trait of knuckle-walking.
gossip: Someone who likes to talk about other people's private or personal business.
governance: The process, or the power, of governing; government or administration.
government: The body with the power to make and/or enforce laws to control a country, land area, people or organization.

grain: The harvested seeds of various grass food crops eg: wheat, corn, barley.
gram: A unit of mass equal to one-thousandth of a kilogram. Symbol: g

grand: (plural "grand") A thousand of some unit of currency, such as dollars or pounds. (Compare G.)
grandparent: To be, or act as, a grandfather to.

grapefruit: The tree of the species Citrus paradisi, a hybrid of pomelo (Citrus maxima) and sweet orange.
graph: (applied mathematics) A data chart (graphical representation of data) intended to illustrate the relationship between a set (or sets) of numbers (quantities, measurements or indicative numbers) and a reference set, whose elements are indexed to those of the former set(s) and may or may not be numbers.

grassland: An area dominated by grass or grasslike vegetation.
gravel: Small fragments of rock, used for laying on the beds of roads and railways, and as ballast.
gravitas: Seriousness in bearing or manner; dignity
gravity: The state or condition of having weight; weight; heaviness.

gray: An achromatic colour intermediate between black and white.
grease: Animal fat in a melted or soft state
greatness: The state, condition, or quality of being great
greed: A selfish or excessive desire for more than is needed or deserved, especially of money, wealth, food, or other possessions.

grin: A smile in which the lips are parted to reveal the teeth.
grip: To take hold of, particularly with the hand.

grocery: (usually groceries) retail foodstuffs and other household supplies.
ground: The surface of the Earth, as opposed to the sky or water or underground.
group: A number of things or persons being in some relation to one another.

growth: An increase in size, number, value, or strength.
grub: An immature stage in the life cycle of an insect; a larva.

guarantee: Anything that assures a certain outcome.
guard: A person who, or thing that, protects or watches over something.

guerrilla: A soldier in a small independent group, fighting against the government or regular forces by surprise raids.
guess: To reach a partly (or totally) unqualified conclusion.
guest: A recipient of hospitality, specifically someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
guestbook: A type of ledger in which visitors to a particular establishment, such as a bed and breakfast or a museum, may leave comments about the establishment.
guidance: The act or process of guiding.

guilder: The former currency unit in the Netherlands, divided into 100 cents.
guilty: A plea by a defendant who does not contest a charge.

gum: (often in the plural) The flesh around the teeth.

hackwork: Work, usually of a professional nature, either repetitive or done to a formula.
hail: Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
hair: A pigmented filament of keratin which grows from a follicle on the skin of humans and other mammals.

halt: To limp; move with a limping gait.
ham: The region back of the knee joint; the popliteal space; the hock.

hammer: A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
hammock: A swinging couch or bed, usually made of netting or canvas about six feet wide, suspended by clews or cords at the ends.
hamster: Any of various Old-World rodent species belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae.
hand: The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in a human, and the corresponding part in many other animals.

handful: The amount that a hand will grasp or contain.

handicap: Something that prevents, hampers, or hinders.
handle: The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.

handmaiden: A maid that waits at hand; a female servant or attendant.
handover: The transference of authority, control, power or knowledge from one agency to another, or from one state to another.
handrail: A rail which can be held, such as on the side of a staircase, ramp or other walkway, and serving as a support or guard.
handsaw: A saw small enough to be used by one hand.
hanger: One who hangs, or causes to be hanged; a hangman, paper hanger, etc.
happiness: The emotion of being happy; joy.
hardcover: A book with a rigid binding, often of cardboard or leather.
hardening: To become hard (tough, resistant to pressure).
hardhat: A helmet, usually made from rigid plastic, used on construction sites to protect the head from falling objects.
hardware: Fixtures, equipment, tools and devices used for general-purpose construction and repair of a structure or object. Also such equipment as sold as stock by a store of the same name, e.g. hardware store.
hare: Any of several plant-eating animals of the family Leporidae, especially of the genus Lepus, similar to a rabbit, but larger and with longer ears.
harmonica: A musical wind instrument with a series of holes for the player to blow into, each hole producing a different note
harp: A musical instrument consisting of a body and a curved neck, strung with strings of varying length that are stroked or plucked with the fingers and are vertical to the soundboard when viewed from the end of the body

harvest: The third season of the year; autumn; fall.
harvester: A person who gathers the harvest.
hash: Food, especially meat and potatoes, chopped and mixed together.
hashtag: A metadata tag, signaled by a preceding hash sign (#), used to label content.
hassock: A dense clump of grass or vegetation; a tussock.
hat: A covering for the head, often in the approximate form of a cone or a cylinder closed at its top end, and sometimes having a brim and other decoration.
hatbox: A piece of luggage for a hat; a case or box for a hat.
hatchet: A small light axe with a short handle; a tomahawk.
hatchling: A newly hatched bird, reptile or other animal that has emerged from an egg.
