pulley: One of the simple machines; a sheave, a wheel with a grooved rim, in which a pulled rope or chain lifts an object (more useful when two or more pulleys are used together, as in a block and tackle arrangement, such that a small force moving through a greater distance can exert a larger force through a smaller distance).
pulse: A normally regular beat felt when arteries are depressed, caused by the pumping action of the heart.
puma: The mountain lion or cougar, Puma concolor.
pump: A device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas.
pumpernickel: A German sourdough bread made from rye.
pumpkin: A domesticated plant, in species Cucurbita pepo, similar in growth pattern, foliage, flower, and fruit to the squash or melon.
pun: A joke or type of wordplay in which similar definitions or sounds of two words or phrases, or different definitions of the same word, are deliberately confused.
punch: A hit or strike with one's fist.
punctuation: A set of symbols and marks which are used to clarify meaning in text by separating strings of words into clauses, phrases and sentences.
punishment: The act or process of punishing, imposing and/or applying a sanction.
pup: A young dog, wolf, fox, seal, or shark, or the young of certain other animals.
pupa: An insect in the development stage between larva and adult.
pupil: A learner under the supervision of a teacher or professor.
puppet: Any small model of a person or animal able to be moved by strings or rods, or in the form of a glove.
puppy: A young dog, especially before sexual maturity (12-18 months)
purchase: The acquisition of title to, or property in, anything for a price; buying for money or its equivalent.
purity: The state or degree of being pure.
purple: A colour/color that is a dark blend of red and blue; dark magenta.
purpose: An objective to be reached; a target; an aim; a goal.
purr: The vibrating sound made by a cat in its throat when contented.
purse: A small bag for carrying money.
push: A short, directed application of force; an act of pushing.
put: A right to sell something at a predetermined price.
puzzle: Anything that is difficult to understand or make sense of.
pyramid: An ancient massive construction with a square or rectangular base and four triangular sides meeting in an apex, such as those built as tombs in Egypt or as bases for temples in Mesoamerica.
pyridine: Any of a class of aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a ring of five carbon atoms and an nitrogen atom; especially the simplest one, C5H5N.
quadrant: One of the four sections made by dividing an area with two perpendicular lines.
quail: To waste away; to fade, to wither
qualification: The act or process of qualifying for a position, achievement etc.
quantity: A fundamental, generic term used when referring to the measurement (count, amount) of a scalar, vector, number of items or to some other way of denominating the value of a collection or group of items.
quart: A unit of liquid capacity equal to two pints; one-fourth (quarter) of a gallon. Equivalent to 1.136 liters in the UK and 0.946 liter (liquid quart) or 1.101 liters (dry quart) in the U.S.
quartet: A music composition in four parts, each performed by a single voice or instrument.
quartz: The most abundant mineral on the earth's surface, of chemical composition silicon dioxide, SiO2. It occurs in a variety of forms, both crystalline and amorphous. Found in every environment.
queen: A female monarch. Example: Queen Victoria.
query: A question, an inquiry (US), an enquiry (UK).
quest: A journey or effort in pursuit of a goal (often lengthy, ambitious, or fervent); a mission.
question: A sentence, phrase or word which asks for information, reply or response; an interrogative.
questioner: A person who asks questions, or who conducts an official enquiry.
questionnaire: A form containing a list of questions; a means of gathering information for a survey
quiche: A pie made primarily of eggs and cream in a pastry crust. Other ingredients such as chopped meat or vegetables are often added to the eggs before the quiche is baked.
quicksand: Wet sand that things readily sink in, often found near rivers or coasts
quill: The lower shaft of a feather, specifically the region lacking barbs.
quilt: A bed covering consisting of two layers of fabric stitched together, with insulation between, often having a decorative design.
quince: The pear-shaped fruit of a small tree of the rose family, Cydonia oblonga.
quinoa: A goosefoot (Chenopodium quinoa) native to the Andes and cultivated for its edible seeds.
quiver: A container for arrows, crossbow bolts or darts, such as those fired from a bow, crossbow or blowgun.
quota: A proportional part or share; the share or proportion assigned to each in a division.
quotation: A fragment of a human expression that is repeated by somebody else. Most often a quotation is taken from literature or speech, but also scenes from a movie, elements of a painting, a passage of music, etc., may be quoted.
quote: A quotation; a statement attributed to a person.
rabbi: A Jewish scholar or teacher of halacha (Jewish law), capable of making halachic decisions.
rabbit: A mammal of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail.
raccoon: A nocturnal omnivore native to North America, typically with a mixture of gray, brown, and black fur, a mask-like marking around the eyes and a striped tail; Procyon lotor.
race: A contest between people, animals, vehicles, etc. where the goal is to be the first to reach some objective. Example: Several horses run in a horse race, and the first one to reach the finishing post wins
racer: Someone who takes part in a race.
racing: To take part in a race (in the sense of a contest).
racism: Belief that there are distinct human races with inherent differences which determine their abilities, and generally that some are superior and others inferior.
racist: A person who believes in or supports racism; a person who believes that a particular race is superior to others.
rack: A series of one or more shelves, stacked one above the other
radar: A method of detecting distant objects and determining their position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysis of sent radio waves (usually microwaves) reflected from their surfaces
radiator: Anything which radiates or emits rays.
radio: The technology that allows for the transmission of sound or other signals by modulation of electromagnetic waves.
radiosonde: A miniature radio carried aloft by an unmanned balloon to automatically transmit measurements of the upper air such as the wind speed, pressure, temperature, and relative humidity to a receiving station on the ground.
radish: A plant of the Brassicaceae family, Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus, having an edible root.
raffle: A drawing, often held as a fundraiser, in which tickets or chances are sold to win a prize.
raft: A flat-bottomed craft able to float and drift on water, used for transport or as a waterborne platform.
raid: A quick hostile or predatory incursion or invasion in a battle.
rail: A horizontal bar extending between supports and used for support or as a barrier; a railing.
railroad: A permanent road consisting of fixed metal rails to drive trains or similar motorized vehicles on.
railway: A transport system using rails used to move passengers or goods.
rain: Condensed water falling from a cloud.
rainbow: A multicoloured arch in the sky, produced by prismatic refraction of light within droplets of rain in the air.
raincoat: A waterproof coat to be worn in the rain.
rainmaker: Someone or something that causes or attempts to cause rain to fall.
rainstorm: A storm characterized by substantial, heavy rainfall.
raise: An increase in wages or salary; a rise (UK).
rake: A garden tool with a row of pointed teeth fixed to a long handle, used for collecting debris, grass, etc., for flattening the ground, or for loosening soil; also, a similar wheel-mounted tool drawn by a horse or a tractor.
rally: A public gathering or mass meeting that is not mainly a protest and is organized to inspire enthusiasm for a cause.
ramen: Soup noodles of wheat, with various ingredients (Japanese style)
ramie: (usually countable) A tall, tropical Asian perennial herb, Boehmeria nivea, cultivated for its fibrous stems.
ranch: A large plot of land used for raising cattle, sheep or other livestock.
rancher: A person who operates a ranch.
range: A line or series of mountains, buildings, etc.
rank: Strong of its kind or in character; unmitigated; virulent; thorough; utter (used of negative things).
rap: A sharp blow with something hard.
rat: A medium-sized rodent belonging to the genus Rattus.
ratepayer: Someone who pays for utility service
rating: To assign or be assigned a particular rank or level.
ratio: A number representing a comparison between two named things.
rationale: An explanation of the basis or fundamental reasons for something.
rations: A portion of some limited resource allocated to a person or group.
raven: Any of several, generally large and lustrous black species of birds in the genus Corvus, especially the common raven, Corvus corax.
ravioli: Small square parcels of pasta filled with meat, cheese, spinach etc.
ray: A beam of light or radiation.
razor: A keen-edged knife of peculiar shape, used in shaving the hair from the face or other parts of the body.
reach: The act of stretching or extending; extension.
reactant: Any of the participants present at the start of a chemical reaction
reaction: An action or statement in response to a stimulus or other event.
read: A reading or an act of reading, especially an actor's part of a play.
readiness: The state or degree of being ready; preparedness.
reading: To look at and interpret letters or other information that is written.
reality: The state of being actual or real.
realm: An abstract sphere of influence, real or imagined.
reamer: A tool for boring a hole wider.
rear: To bring up to maturity, as offspring; to educate; to instruct; to foster.
reasoning: To deduce or come to a conclusion by being rational
rebel: A person who resists an established authority, often violently
rebellion: Armed resistance to an established government or ruler.
recall: The action or fact of calling someone or something back.
recapitulation: A subsequent brief recitement or enumeration of the major points in a narrative, article, or book.
receipt: The act of receiving, or the fact of having been received.
receiver: A person who or thing that receives or is intended to receive something. More formal, usually referring to one who receives such things as an award or medal.
receptor: A protein on a cell wall that binds with specific molecules so that they can be absorbed into the cell in order to control certain functions.
recession: The act or an instance of receding or withdrawing.
recipe: A formula for preparing or using a medicine; a prescription; also, a medicine prepared from such instructions.
reciprocity: The characteristic of being reciprocal, e.g. of a relationship between people.
reclamation: The act of reclaiming or the state of being reclaimed.
recliner: One who, or that which, reclines.
recognition: The act of recognizing or the condition of being recognized (matching a current observation with a memory of a prior observation of the same entity)
recollection: The act of recollecting, or recalling to the memory; the act of recalling to memory
reconsideration: The act of reconsidering or something reconsidered
record: A disk, usually made of a polymer, used to record sound for playback on a phonograph.
recorder: An apparatus for recording; a device which records.
recording: To make a record of information.
recovery: The act or process of regaining or repossession of something lost.
recreation: Any activity, such as play, that amuses, diverts or stimulates.
recruit: A supply of anything wasted or exhausted; a reinforcement.
rectangle: A quadrilateral having opposing sides parallel and four right angles.
red: Any of a range of colours having the longest wavelengths, 670 nm, of the visible spectrum; a primary additive colour for transmitted light: the colour obtained by subtracting green and blue from white light using magenta and yellow filters; the colour of blood, ripe strawberries, etc.
redesign: A plan for making changes to the structure and functions of an artifact, building or system so as to better serve the purpose of the original design, or to serve purposes different from those set forth in the original design.
reduction: The act, process, or result of reducing.
reef: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
refectory: A dining-hall, especially in an institution such as a college or monastery.
referendum: A direct popular vote on a proposed law or constitutional amendment. The adposition on is usually used before the related subject of the vote.
reflection: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
reform: The change of something that is defective, broken, inefficient or otherwise negative, in order to correct or improve it
refreshments: The action of refreshing; a means of restoring strength, energy or vigour.
refrigerator: A household appliance used for keeping food fresh by refrigeration (short form fridge).
refuge: A state of safety, protection or shelter.
refuse: Collectively, items or material that have been discarded; rubbish, garbage.
region: Any considerable and connected part of a space or surface; specifically, a tract of land or sea of considerable but indefinite extent; a country; a district; in a broad sense, a place without special reference to location or extent but viewed as an entity for geographical, social or cultural reasons.
regionalism: Affection, often excessive, for one's own region and to everything related to it.
register: A machine that tabulates the amount of sales transactions, makes a permanent and cumulative record of them, and has a drawer in which cash can be kept.
registration: The act of signing up or registering for something.
registry: A building in which things are registered or where registers are kept.
regret: Emotional pain on account of something done or experienced in the past, with a wish that it had been different; a looking back with dissatisfaction or with longing.
regulation: The act of regulating or the condition of being regulated.
regulator: A device that controls or limits something.
reindeer: (plural: reindeer) Any Arctic and subarctic-dwelling deer of the species Rangifer tarandus, with a number of subspecies.
relation: The manner in which two things may be associated.
relationship: Connection or association; the condition of being related.
relative: Someone in the same family; someone connected by blood, marriage, or adoption.
relaxation: The act of relaxing or the state of being relaxed; the opposite of stress or tension; the aim of recreation and leisure activities.
release: The event of setting (someone or something) free (e.g. hostages, slaves, prisoners, caged animals, hooked or stuck mechanisms).
reliability: The quality of being reliable, dependable or trustworthy.
relief: The removal of stress or discomfort.
religion: Belief in a spiritual or metaphysical reality (often including at least one deity), accompanied by practices or rituals pertaining to the belief.
remains: (chiefly in the plural) That which is left; relic; remainder.
remark: An act of pointing out or noticing; notice or observation.
remnant: The small portion remaining of a larger thing or group.
remote: An element of broadcast programming originating away from the station's or show's control room.
removal: The process of moving, or the fact of being removed.
rent: A payment made by a tenant at intervals in order to occupy a property.
reorganisation: The act or process of rearranging. See reorganize.
reorganization: The act or process of rearranging. See reorganize.
reparation: (usually in the plural) A payment of time, effort or money to undo past transgression(s).
replacement: A person or thing that takes the place of another; a substitute.
replication: The process by which an object, person, place or idea may be copied mimicked or reproduced.
reply: A written or spoken response; part of a conversation.
report: A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).
reporting: To relate details of (an event or incident); to recount, describe (something).
repository: A location for storage, often for safety or preservation.
republic: A state where sovereignty rests with the people or their representatives, rather than with a monarch or emperor; a country with no monarchy.
republican: Someone who favors a republic as a form of government.
request: Act of requesting (with the adposition at in the presence of possessives, and on in their absence).
requirement: A necessity or prerequisite; something required or obligatory. Its adpositions are generally of in relation to who or what has given it, on in relation to whom or what it is given to, and for in relation to what is required.
resale: The action of selling something previously bought, usually at a higher price for profit.
rescue: An act or episode of rescuing, saving.
research: Diligent inquiry or examination to seek or revise facts, principles, theories, applications, etc.; laborious or continued search after truth.
resemblance: The quality or state of resembling
reservation: The act of reserving, withholding or keeping back.
reservoir: A place where anything is kept in store
reset: To set back to the initial state.
residence: The place where one lives; one's home.
resident: A person, animal or plant living at a certain location or in a certain area.
residue: Whatever remains after something else has been removed.
resistance: The act of resisting, or the capacity to resist.
resort: A place where people go for recreation, especially one with facilities such as lodgings, entertainment, and a relaxing environment.
resource: Something that one uses to achieve an objective, e.g. raw materials or personnel.
respect: An attitude of consideration or high regard
respite: A brief interval of rest or relief.
response: An answer or reply, or something in the nature of an answer or reply.
responsibility: The state of being responsible, accountable, or answerable.
rest: (of a person or animal) Relief from work or activity by sleeping; sleep.
restaurant: An eating establishment in which diners are served food, usually by waiters at their tables but sometimes (as in a fast food restaurant) at a counter.
restoration: The process of bringing an object back to its original state; the process of restoring something.
restriction: The act of restricting, or the state of being restricted.
restroom: A room containing a public toilet: a public lavatory.
result: That which results; the conclusion or end to which any course or condition of things leads, or which is obtained by any process or operation; consequence or effect.
retailer: A retail sales company or salesman.
retention: The act of retaining or something retained
rethinking: To think again about a problem.
retina: The thin layer of cells at the back of the eyeball where light is converted into neural signals sent to the brain.
retouching: To improve something (especially a photograph), by adding or correcting details, or by removing flaws.
retreat: The act of pulling back or withdrawing, as from something dangerous, or unpleasant.
retrospective: An exhibition of works from an extended period of an artist's activity.
reunion: The process or act of reuniting.
reveal: The outer side of a window or door frame; the jamb.
revelation: The act of revealing or disclosing.
revenant: Someone who returns from a long absence.
revenge: Any form of personal retaliatory action against an individual, institution, or group for some alleged or perceived harm or injustice.
revenue: The income returned by an investment.
review: A second or subsequent reading of a text or artifact in an attempt to gain new insights.
revival: The act of reviving, or the state of being revived
revolution: A political upheaval in a government or nation state characterized by great change.
revolver: A handgun with a revolving chamber enabling several shots to be fired without reloading.
reward: Something of value given in return for an act.
rhetoric: The art of using language, especially public speaking, as a means to persuade.
rheumatism: Any disorder of the muscles, tendons, joints, bones, nerves, characterized by pain, discomfort and disability.
rhinoceros: Any of several large herbivorous pachyderms native to Africa and Asia of the five extant species in the three extant genera in the family Rhinocerotidae, with thick, gray skin and one or two horns on their snouts.
rhubarb: Any plant of the genus Rheum, especially Rheum rhabarbarum, having large leaves and long green or reddish acidic leafstalks that are edible, in particular when cooked (although the leaves are mildly poisonous).
rhythm: The variation of strong and weak elements (such as duration, accent) of sounds, notably in speech or music, over time; a beat or meter.
rib: Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum
ribbon: A long, narrow strip of timber bent and bolted longitudinally to the ribs of a vessel, to hold them in position and give rigidity to the framework.
rice: Cereal plants, Oryza sativa of the grass family whose seeds are used as food.
riddle: A verbal puzzle, mystery, or other problem of an intellectual nature.
rider: One who rides, often on a horse or a motorcycle.
ridge: The back of any animal; especially the upper or projecting part of the back of a quadruped.
riding: To transport oneself by sitting on and directing a horse, later also a bicycle etc.
rifle: A shouldered firearm with a long, rifled barrel to improve range and accuracy.
rim: An edge around something, especially when circular.
ring: (physical) A solid object in the shape of a circle.
ringworm: A contagious fungal infection of the skin, characterised by ring-shaped discoloured patches, covered by vesicles or scales.
riot: Wanton or unrestrained behavior; uproar; tumult.
ripple: A moving disturbance, or undulation, in the surface of a fluid.
rise: To move, or appear to move, physically upwards relative to the ground.
risk: A possible adverse event or outcome
ritual: Rite; a repeated set of actions
river: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
riverbed: The path where a river runs, or where a river once ran; the bottom earthen part of a river, not including the riverbanks.
rivulet: A small brook or stream; a streamlet.
road: A way used for travelling between places, originally one wide enough to allow foot passengers and horses to travel, now (US) usually one surfaced with asphalt or concrete and designed to accommodate many vehicles travelling in both directions. In the UK both senses are heard: a country road is the same as a country lane.
roadway: A way used as a road.
roar: A long, loud, deep shout, as of rage or laughter, made with the mouth wide open.
roast: A cut of meat suited to roasting
robe: A long loose outer garment, often signifying honorary stature.
robin: Any of various passerine birds (about 100 species) of the families Muscicapidae, Turdidae and Petroicidae (formerly Eopsaltriidae), typically with a red breast.
robot: A machine built to carry out some complex task or group of tasks by physically moving, especially one which can be programmed.
robotics: The science and technology of robots, their design, manufacture, and application
rocker: A curved piece of wood attached to the bottom of a rocking chair or cradle that enables it to rock back and forth.
rod: A straight, round stick, shaft, bar, cane, or staff.
role: A character or part played by a performer or actor.
roll: The act or result of rolling, or state of being rolled.
romaine: Lactuca sativa var. longifolia, a type of lettuce having long crisp leaves forming a slender head.
romance: A story relating to chivalry; a story involving knights, heroes, adventures, quests, etc.
roof: The external covering at the top of a building.
roommate: A person with whom one shares a room, as at university etc.
rooster: A male domestic chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) or other gallinaceous bird.
root: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
rope: Thick strings, yarn, monofilaments, metal wires, or strands of other cordage that are twisted together to form a stronger line.
rose: A shrub of the genus Rosa, with red, pink, white or yellow flowers.
rosemary: A shrub, Rosmarinus officinalis, that originates from Europe and Asia Minor and produces a fragrant herb used in cooking and perfumes.
roster: A list of individuals or groups, usually for an organization of some kind such as military officers and enlisted personnel enrolled in a particular unit; a muster roll; a sports team, with the names of players who are eligible to be placed in the lineup for a particular game; or a list of students officially enrolled in a school or class.
rostrum: A dais, pulpit, or similar platform for a speaker, conductor, or other performer.
rotation: The act of turning around a centre or an axis.
round: So as to form a circle or trace a circular path, or approximation thereof.
roundabout: (Australia and sometimes United States) A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.
route: A course or way which is traveled or passed.
router: Someone who routes or directs items from one location to another.
routine: A course of action to be followed regularly; a standard procedure.
row: A line of objects, often regularly spaced, such as seats in a theatre, vegetable plants in a garden etc.
rowboat: A small open boat propelled by oars (by rowing).
rowing: To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
rubber: Pliable material derived from the sap of the rubber tree; a hydrocarbon polymer of isoprene.
rubric: A heading in a book highlighted in red.
ruby: A clear, deep, red variety of corundum, valued as a precious stone.
rudiment: (often in the plural) A fundamental principle or skill, especially in a field of learning.
ruffle: Any gathered or curled strip of fabric added as trim or decoration.
rug: A partial covering for a floor.
rugby: (usually uncountable) A form of football in which players can hold or kick an ovoid ball. The ball cannot be handled forwards and points are scored by touching the ball to the ground in the area past their opponent’s territory or kicking the ball between goalposts and over a crossbar.
ruin: (sometimes in the plural) The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
ruler: A (usually rigid), flat, rectangular measuring or drawing device with graduations in units of measurement; a straightedge with markings.
ruling: To regulate, be in charge of, make decisions for, reign over.
rum: A distilled spirit derived from fermented cane sugar and molasses.
rumor: A statement or claim of questionable accuracy, from no known reliable source, usually spread by word of mouth.
runaway: A person or animal that runs away or has run away; a person, animal, or organization that escapes captivity or restrictions.
runner: Act or instance of running, of moving rapidly using the feet.
runway: A defined, narrow section of land or an artificial structure used for access.
rush: Any of several stiff plants of the genus Juncus, or the family Juncaceae, having hollow or pithy stems and small flowers, and often growing in marshes or near water.
rust: The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation.
rutabaga: The swede, or Swedish turnip; the European plant Brassica napus var. napobrassica
rye: A grain used extensively in Europe for making bread, beer, and (now generally) for animal fodder.
sabre: A light sword, sharp along the front edge, part of the back edge, and at the point.
sac: A bag or pouch inside a plant or animal that typically contains a fluid.
sack: A bag; especially a large bag of strong, coarse material for storage and handling of various commodities, such as potatoes, coal, coffee; or, a bag with handles used at a supermarket, a grocery sack; or, a small bag for small items, a satchel.
saddle: A seat (tack) for a rider placed on the back of a horse or other animal.
sadness: The state or emotion of being sad.
safari: A trip into any undeveloped area to see, photograph or hunt wild animals in their own environment.
safe: A box, usually made of metal, in which valuables can be locked for safekeeping.
safeguard: Something that serves as a guard or protection; a defense.
safety: The condition or feeling of being safe; security; certainty.
saffron: The plant Crocus sativus, a crocus.
sage: A wise person or spiritual teacher; someone of gravity and wisdom, especially, a teacher venerable for years, and of sound judgment and prudence; a grave or stoic philosopher.
sail: A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the boat via a combination of mast, spars and ropes.
sailboat: A boat propelled by a sail.
sailing: To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water; to be impelled on a body of water by steam or other power.
sailor: A person in the business of navigating ships or other vessels
saint: A person whom a church or another religious group has officially recognised as especially holy or godly; one eminent for piety and virtue.
salad: A food made primarily of a mixture of raw or cold ingredients, typically vegetables, usually served with a dressing such as vinegar or mayonnaise.
salami: A large cured meat sausage of Italian origin, served in slices.
salary: A fixed amount of money paid to a worker, usually calculated on a monthly or annual basis, not hourly, as wages. Implies a degree of professionalism and/or autonomy.
salesman: A man whose job it is to sell things, either in a shop/store or elsewhere.
salmon: One of several species of fish, typically of the Salmoninae subfamily, brownish above with silvery sides and delicate pinkish-orange flesh; they ascend rivers to spawn.
salon: A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.
saloon: A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.
salsa: A spicy tomato sauce, often including onions and hot peppers.
salt: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
salute: An utterance or gesture expressing greeting or honor towards someone, now especially a formal, non-verbal gesture made with the arms or hands in any of various specific positions.
samovar: A metal urn with a spigot, for boiling water for making tea. Traditionally, the water is heated by hot coals or charcoal in a chimney-like tube which runs through the center of the urn. Today, it is more likely that the water is heated by an electric coil.
sampan: A flat-bottomed Chinese wooden boat propelled by two oars.
sample: A part or snippet of something taken or presented for inspection, or shown as evidence of the quality of the whole; a specimen.
samurai: In feudal Japan, a soldier who served a daimyo.
sanction: An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.
sanctity: Holiness of life or disposition; saintliness
sanctuary: A place of safety, refuge or protection.
sand: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
sandal: A type of open shoe made up of straps or bands holding a sole to the foot
sandbar: A ridge of sand caused by the action of waves along a shore.
sandpaper: A strong paper coated with sand, ground glass, or other abrasive material for smoothing and polishing.
sandwich: A dish or foodstuff where two or more slices of bread serve as the wrapper or container of some other food.
sardine: Any one of several species of small herring which are commonly preserved in olive oil or in tins for food, especially the pilchard, or European sardine Sardina pilchardus (syn.
