tart: Sharp to the taste; acid; sour.
task: A piece of work done as part of one’s duties.
tassel: A ball-shaped bunch of plaited or otherwise entangled threads from which at one end protrudes a cord on which the ball is hung, and which may have loose, dangling threads at the other end (often used as decoration along the bottom of garments, curtains or other hangings).
taste: One of the sensations produced by the tongue in response to certain chemicals; the quality of giving this sensation.
tatami: Straw matting, in a standard size, used as a floor covering in Japanese houses
tattler: One who tattles (notifies authorities of illicit behavior) or is inclined to do so; a tattletale.
tattoo: An image made in the skin with ink and a needle.
tavern: A building containing a bar licensed to sell alcoholic drinks, and usually offering accommodation; an inn.
tax: Money paid to the government other than for transaction-specific goods and services.
taxi: A vehicle that may be hired for single journeys by members of the public, driven by a taxi driver.
taxicab: A vehicle that passengers hire to take them between locations of their choice, the fare being calculated with a taximeter; a taxi or cab
taxpayer: A person who is subject to, liable for, or pays tax as opposed to a nontaxpayer who is neither the subject nor the object of revenue laws.
tea: A drug smoked or ingested for euphoric effect, cannabis.
teacher: A person who teaches, especially one employed in a school.
teaching: Something taught by a religious or philosophical authority.
team: A set of draught animals, such as two horses in front of a carriage.
teammate: One who is on the same team.
teapot: A vessel for brewing and serving tea.
tear: A hole or break caused by tearing.
technician: A person who studies or practises technology.
technique: The practical aspects of a given art, occupation etc.; formal requirements.
technologist: A scientist or an engineer who specializes in a particular technology, or who uses technology in a particular field.
technology: The organization of knowledge for practical purposes.
tectonics: The study of crustal plates and other large-scale structural features of the Earth.
teenager: A person between 13 and 19 years of age; an adolescent.
teepee: To toilet paper; to throw toilet paper in rolls over a structure, so the structure becomes draped with it.
telephone: A telecommunication device (originally mechanical, and now electronic) used for two-way talking with another person (now often shortened to phone).
telescreen: A screen for broadcasting television or similar media.
television: An electronic communication medium that allows the transmission of real-time visual images, and often sound.
tell: A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a poker game or police interrogation), that reveals information that the person exhibiting the behavior is attempting to withhold.
teller: A device that provides bank customers with cash withdrawal and other services without the need for a human teller.
temper: A tendency to be in a certain type of mood; a habitual way of thinking, behaving or reacting.
temperature: A measure of cold or heat, often measurable with a thermometer.
temporary: One serving for a limited time; short-term employee.
temptress: An alluring woman who seduces or exploits men.
tenant: One who pays a fee (rent) in return for the use of land, buildings, or other property owned by others.
tendency: A likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction; a tending toward.
tenement: A building that is rented to multiple tenants, especially a low-rent, run-down one.
tenet: An opinion, belief, or principle that is held as absolute truth by someone or especially an organization.
tennis: A sport played by two players (or four in doubles), who alternately strike the ball over a net using racquets.
tenor: A musical range or section higher than bass and lower than alto.
tension: The condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other.
tensor: A muscle that stretches a part, or renders it tense.
tent: A pavilion or portable lodge consisting of skins, canvas, or some strong cloth, stretched and sustained by poles, used for sheltering people from the weather.
tentacle: An elongated, boneless, flexible organ or limb of some animals, such as the octopus and squid.
tenth: The person or thing coming next after the ninth in a series; that which is in the tenth position.
teriyaki: A cooking technique used in Japanese cuisine in which foods are broiled or grilled in a sweet soy sauce marinade.
term: That which limits the extent of anything; limit, extremity, bound, boundary.
terminal: A building in an airport where passengers transfer from ground transportation to the facilities that allow them to board airplanes.
termination: The process of terminating or the state of being terminated.
terminology: The doctrine of terms; a theory of terms or appellations; a treatise on terms, a system of specialized terms.
termite: A white-bodied, wood-consuming insect of the infraorder Isoptera, in the order Blattodea.
terrace: A platform that extends outwards from a building.
terracotta: A hard red-brown unglazed earthenware, used for pottery and building construction.
terrapin: Any of several small turtles, of the families Emydidae and Geoemydidae, that live in fresh or brackish water.
terrarium: An enclosure wherein very small animals are displayed humanely, often with some plants, in a naturalistic setting.
territory: A large extent or tract of land; for example a region, country or district.
terrorism: The deliberate commission of an act of violence to create public fear through the suffering of the victims in the furtherance of a political or social agenda.
terrorist: A person, group, or organization that uses violent action, or the threat of violent action, to further political goals.
testament: A solemn, authentic instrument in writing, by which a person declares his or her will as to disposal of his or her inheritance (estate and effects) after his or her death, benefiting specified heir(s).
testimonial: A statement, especially one given under oath; testimony
testimony: Statements made by a witness in court.
text: A writing consisting of multiple glyphs, characters, symbols or sentences.
textbook: A coursebook, a formal manual of instruction in a specific subject, especially one for use in schools or colleges.
texture: The feel or shape of a surface or substance; the smoothness, roughness, softness, etc. of something.
thanks: An expression of appreciation; a thought.
thaw: The melting of ice, snow, or other congealed matter; the resolution of ice, or the like, into the state of a fluid; liquefaction by heat of anything congealed by frost
theater: A place or building, consisting of a stage and seating, in which an audience gathers to watch plays, musical performances, public ceremonies, and so on.
theism: Belief in the existence of at least one deity.
theme: A subject of a talk or an artistic piece; a topic.
theology: The study of God, a god, or gods; and of the truthfulness of religion in general.
theory: A description of an event or system that is considered to be accurate.
therapist: Someone who provides therapy, usually professionally.
therapy: Attempted remediation of a health problem following a diagnosis, usually synonymous with treatment.
thermals: A column of rising air in the lower atmosphere created by uneven heating of Earth's surface.
thermometer: An apparatus used to measure temperature.
thermostat: A device that automatically responds to changes in temperature by activating a heating or cooling system to maintain the temperature at a desired setting.
thesis: Senses relating to logic, rhetoric, etc.
thickness: The property of being thick (in dimension).
thief: One who carries out a theft.
thigh: The upper leg of a human, between the hip and the knee.
thing: That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, object, quality or concept.
thirst: A sensation of dryness in the throat associated with a craving for liquids, produced by deprivation of drink, or by some other cause (such as fear, excitement, etc.) which spots the secretion of the pharyngeal mucous membrane
thistle: Any of several perennial composite plants, especially of genera Cirsium, Carduus, Cynara, or Onopordum, having prickly leaves and showy flower heads with prickly bracts.
thorn: A sharp protective spine of a plant.
thought: To ponder, to go over in one's head.
thread: A long, thin and flexible form of material, generally with a round cross-section, used in sewing, weaving or in the construction of string.
threat: An expression of intent to injure or punish another.
threshold: The bottom-most part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
thrift: The characteristic of using a minimum of something (especially money).
thrill: A trembling or quivering, especially one caused by emotion.
throat: The front part of the neck.
throne: An impressive seat used by a monarch, often on a raised dais in a throne room and reserved for formal occasions.
thrush: Any of several species of songbirds of the family Turdidae, often with spotted underbellies such as the bluebird, nightingale, and American robin have.
thrust: An attack made by moving the sword parallel to its length and landing with the point.
thug: Someone with an intimidating and unseemly appearance and mannerisms, who treats others violently and roughly, often for hire.
thumb: The short thick digit of the hand that for humans has the most mobility and can be made to oppose (moved to touch) all of the other fingers.
thump: A blow that produces a muffled sound.
thunder: The loud rumbling, cracking, or crashing sound caused by expansion of rapidly heated air around a lightning bolt.
thunderbolt: A flash of lightning accompanied by a crash of thunder.
thunderhead: The top portion of a cumulonimbus cloud, which tends to be flattened or fibery in appearance, and may be indicative of thunderstorm activity.
thunderstorm: A storm consisting of thunder and lightning produced by a cumulonimbus, usually accompanied with heavy rain, wind, and sometimes hail; and in rarer cases sleet, freezing rain, or snow.
thyme: Any plant of the labiate genus Thymus, such as the garden thyme, Thymus vulgaris, a warm, pungent aromatic, that is much used to give a relish to seasoning and soups.
tic: A sudden, nonrhythmic motor movement or vocalization.
tick: A tiny woodland arachnid of the suborder Ixodida.
ticket: A pass entitling the holder to admission to a show, concert, etc.
tide: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
tiger: Panthera tigris, a large predatory mammal of the cat family, indigenous to Asia.
tights: A close-fitting, sheer or non-sheer skin-tight garment worn principally by women and girls that covers the body completely from the waist down, usually including the feet.
tile: A regularly-shaped slab of clay or other material, affixed to cover or decorate a surface, as in a roof-tile, glazed tile, stove tile, carpet tile etc.
till: Until; to, up to; as late as (a given time).
timbale: A drum-shaped mould used to cook food.
timber: Trees in a forest regarded as a source of wood.
time: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.
timeline: A graphical representation of a chronological sequence of events (past or future); a chronology.
timeout: A short break in the action of a sport, for substitution, consultation, etc.
timetable: A tabular schedule of events with the times at which they occur, especially times of arrivals and departures
timing: To measure or record the time, duration, or rate of.
timpani: The set of precision kettledrums in an orchestra.
tin: A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
tinderbox: A small container containing flint, steel, and tinder (dry, finely-divided fibrous matter), once used to help kindle a fire.
tinkle: A light metallic sound, resembling the tinkling of bells or wind chimes.
tintype: An early, remarkably durable form of photograph (technically a photographic negative), printed on a tin plate, then varnished.
tip: The tip of the external ear.
titanium: A chemical element, atomic number 22; it is a strong, corrosion-resistant transition metal, used to make light alloys for aircraft etc.
title: A prefix (honorific) or suffix (post-nominal) added to a person's name to signify either veneration, official position or a professional or academic qualification. See also
toad: An amphibian, a kind of frog (order Anura) with shorter hindlegs and a drier, wartier skin, many in family Bufonidae.
toaster: One who toasts (cooks lightly by browning).
tobacco: Any plant of the genus Nicotiana.
toe: Each of the five digits on the end of the foot.
toenail: The thin, horny, transparent plate covering the upper surface of the end of a toe.
toffee: A type of confectionery made by boiling sugar (or treacle, etc) with butter or milk, then cooling the mixture so that it becomes hard
tofu: A protein-rich food made from curdled soy milk.
toga: A loose outer garment worn by the citizens of Ancient Rome.
toilet: A covering of linen, silk, or tapestry, spread over a dressing table in a chamber or dressing room.
tolerance: The ability to endure pain or hardship; endurance.
tolerant: Tending to permit, allow, understand, or accept something
toll: Loss or damage incurred through a disaster.
tom-tom: A flat gong (without knob) that is struck with a felt-covered hammer.
tomatillo: A plant of the nightshade family originating in Mexico, Physalis philadelphica, cultivated for its tomato-like green to green-purple fruit surrounded by a thin papery skin.
tomato: A widely cultivated plant, Solanum lycopersicum, having edible fruit.
tomb: A small building (or "vault") for the remains of the dead, with walls, a roof, and (if it is to be used for more than one corpse) a door. It may be partly or wholly in the ground (except for its entrance) in a cemetery, or it may be inside a church proper or in its crypt. Single tombs may be permanently sealed; those for families (or other groups) have doors for access whenever needed.
tomorrow: The day after the present day.
ton: A unit of weight (mass) equal to 2240 pounds (a long ton) or 2000 pounds (a short ton) or 1000 kilograms (a metric ton).
tonality: The system of seven tones built on a tonic key; the 24 major and minor scales.
tongue: The flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into various positions to modify the flow of air from the lungs in order to produce different sounds in speech.
tonic: A substance with medicinal properties intended to restore or invigorate.
tonight: The nighttime of the current day or date; this night.
tool: A mechanical device intended to make a task easier.
toot: The noise of a horn or whistle.
tooth: A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals, generally used for eating.
toothbrush: A brush, used with toothpaste, for cleaning the teeth.
toothpaste: A paste, normally used with a toothbrush, for cleaning the teeth.
toothpick: A small, usually wooden, stick, often pointed at both ends, for removing food residue from between the teeth.
top: The highest or uppermost part of something.
topic: Subject; theme; a category or general area of interest.
topsail: A sail or either of the two sails rigged just above the course sail and supported by the topmast on a square-rigged sailing ship.
toque: A type of hat with no brim.
toreador: A bullfighter, especially one on horseback.
tornado: A violent windstorm characterized by a mobile, twisting, funnel-shaped cloud.
torso: The main part of the (human) body that extends from the neck to the groin, excluding the head and limbs.
torte: A rich, dense cake, typically made with many eggs and relatively little flour (as opposed to a sponge cake or gâteau).
tortellini: Small, ring-shaped pasta, stuffed with meat, cheese etc; eaten with a sauce or in a soup
tortilla: (Mexican cuisine) A flat round bread made out of cornmeal or flour. In Mexican cuisine they are often served with a filling or topping such as frijoles "beans", carne "meat", salsa "sauce", sour cream and cheese; in the latter case they are called quesadillas.
tortoise: Any of various land-dwelling reptiles, of the family Testudinidae or the order Testudines , whose body is enclosed in a shell (carapace plus plastron). The animal can withdraw its head and four legs partially into the shell, providing some protection from predators.
tosser: One who tosses or throws something.
total: An amount obtained by the addition of smaller amounts.
tour: A journey through a particular building, estate, country, etc.
tourism: The act of travelling or sightseeing, particularly away from one's home.
tourist: Someone who travels for pleasure rather than for business.
tournament: During the Middle Ages, a series of battles and other contests designed to prepare knights for war.
towel: A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, as a person after a bath.
tower: A very tall iron-framed structure, usually painted red and white, on which microwave, radio, satellite, or other communication antennas are installed; mast.
town: A settlement; an area with residential districts, shops and amenities, and its own local government; especially one larger than a village and smaller than a city.
toy: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
trachoma: An infectious disease of the eyelid caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.
track: A mark left by something that has passed along.
tracksuit: A garment, usually consisting of a top and trousers (commonly known as tracksuit bottoms) worn as an outer layer by participants in sporting events such as athletics. The tracksuit is usually designed to be easily removed or replaced, before or after competing. Tracksuits have also been adopted in some cultures as leisurewear.
tractor: A vehicle used in farms e.g. for pulling farm equipment and preparing the fields.
trade: Buying and selling of goods and services on a market.
trader: One who earns a living by trading goods or securities.
tradition: A part of culture that is passed from person to person or generation to generation, possibly differing in detail from family to family, such as the way to celebrate holidays.
traditionalism: The adherence to traditional views or practices, especially with regard to cultural or religious matters.
traffic: Pedestrians or vehicles on roads, or the flux or passage thereof.
trafficker: Someone who traffics; a trader or merchant
tragedy: A drama or similar work, in which the main character is brought to ruin or otherwise suffers the extreme consequences of some tragic flaw or weakness of character.
trail: The track or indication marking the route followed by something that has passed, such as the footprints of animal on land or the contrail of an airplane in the sky.
trailer: Someone who or something that trails.
trainer: A person who trains another; a coach.
trait: An identifying characteristic, habit or trend.
tram: A passenger vehicle for public use that runs on tracks in the road (called a streetcar or trolley in North America).
tramp: (sometimes derogatory) A homeless person; a vagabond.
transaction: The act of conducting or carrying out (business, negotiations, plans).
transcript: Something which has been transcribed; a writing or composition consisting of the same words as the original; a written copy.
transfer: The act of conveying or removing something from one place, person or thing to another.
transformation: The act of transforming or the state of being transformed.
transit: The act of passing over, across, or through something.
transition: The process of change from one form, state, style or place to another.
translation: The act of translating, in its various senses:
transmission: The act of transmitting, e.g. data or electric power.
transom: A crosspiece over a door; a lintel.
transparency: The quality of being transparent; transparence.
transplantation: The resettlement of a group of people.
transportation: The act of transporting, or the state of being transported; conveyance, often of people, goods etc.
trap: A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of part of the body.
trapdoor: A hinged or sliding door set into a floor or ceiling.
trapezium: A four-sided polygon with two sides parallel
trapezoid: A (convex) quadrilateral with two (non-adjacent) parallel sides.
trash: Useless things to be discarded; rubbish; refuse.
travel: The act of traveling; passage from place to place.
traveler: A member of a particular nomadic ethnic minority in Ireland, the Pavee.
tray: A small, typically rectangular or round, flat, and rigid object upon which things are carried.
treasure: A collection of valuable things; accumulated wealth; a stock of money, jewels, etc.
treasury: A place where treasure is stored safely.
treat: An entertainment, outing, food, drink, or other indulgence provided by someone for the enjoyment of others.
treatment: The process or manner of treating someone or something.
treaty: A binding agreement concluded by subjects of international law, namely states and international organizations.
tree: Fast growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem.
trellis: An outdoor garden frame that can be used for partitioning a common area.
trench: A long, narrow ditch or hole dug in the ground.
trend: An inclination in a particular direction.
trial: An opportunity to test something out; a test.
triangle: A polygon with three sides and three angles.
tribe: A socially, ethnically, or politically cohesive group of people.
tributary: A natural water stream that flows into a larger river or other body of water.
trick: Something designed to fool or swindle.
trigger: A finger-operated lever used to fire a gun.
trigonometry: The branch of mathematics that deals with the relationships between the sides and the angles of triangles and the calculations based on them, particularly the trigonometric functions.
trillion: (short scale) A million million: 1 followed by twelve zeros, 1012.
trim: Decoration; especially, decoration placed along edges or borders.
trinket: A small showy ornament or piece of jewelry
trip: A journey; an excursion or jaunt
tritone: An interval of three whole tones.
triumph: A conclusive success following an effort, conflict, or confrontation of obstacles; victory; conquest.
trombone: A musical instrument in the brass family, having a cylindrical bore, and usually a sliding tube (but sometimes piston valves, and rarely both). Most often refers to the tenor trombone, which is the most common type of trombone and has a fundamental tone of B♭ˌ (contra B♭).
troop: (collective) A collection of people; a number; a multitude (in general).
trooper: A soldier of private rank in cavalry or armour.
trousers: An article of clothing that covers the part of the body between the waist and the ankles or knees, and is divided into a separate part for each leg.
trout: Any of several species of fish in Salmonidae, closely related to salmon, and distinguished by spawning more than once.
trove: A treasure trove; a collection of treasure.
trowel: A mason’s tool, used in spreading and dressing mortar, and breaking bricks to shape them.
truck: A small wheel or roller, specifically the wheel of a gun carriage.
trumpet: A musical instrument of the brass family, generally tuned to the key of B-flat; by extension, any type of lip-vibrated aerophone, most often valveless and not chromatic.
trust: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
trustee: A person to whom property is legally committed in trust, to be applied either for the benefit of specified individuals, or for public uses; one who is intrusted with property for the benefit of another.
truth: True facts, genuine depiction or statements of reality.
tsunami: A very large and destructive wave, generally caused by a tremendous disturbance in the ocean, such as an undersea earthquake or volcanic eruption. Tsunami are usually a series of waves, or wave train.
tub: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
tuba: A large brass musical instrument, usually in the bass range, played through a vibration of the lips upon the mouthpiece and fingering of the keys.
tube: Anything that is hollow and cylindrical in shape.
tuber: A fleshy, thickened underground stem of a plant, usually containing stored starch, for example a potato or arrowroot.
tugboat: A small, powerful boat used to push or pull barges or to help maneuver larger vessels.
tuition: A sum of money paid for instruction (such as in a high school, boarding school, university, or college).
tulip: A type of flowering plant, genus Tulipa.
tumbler: One who tumbles; one who plays tricks by various motions of the body; an acrobat.
tuna: Any of several species of fish of the genus Thunnus in the family Scombridae.
tune-up: A series of adjustments to an engine in order to improve its performance
tunic: A garment worn over the torso, with or without sleeves, and of various lengths reaching from the hips to the ankles.
turban: A man's headdress made by winding a length of cloth round the head.
turf: A layer of earth covered with grass; sod.
turmeric: An Indian plant, Curcuma longa, with aromatic rhizomes, part of the ginger family (Zingiberaceae).
turn: (heading) to make a non-linear physical movement.
turning: (heading) to make a non-linear physical movement.
turnip: The white root of a yellow-flowered plant, Brassica rapa, grown as a vegetable and as fodder for cattle.
turnover: The amount of money taken as sales transacted in a given period.
turnstile: A rotating mechanical device that controls and counts passage between public areas, especially one that only allows passage after a charge has been paid.
turret: A little tower, frequently a merely ornamental structure at one of the corners of a building or castle.
turtle: Any land or marine reptile of the order Testudines, characterised by a protective shell enclosing its body. See also tortoise.
tusk: One of a pair of elongated pointed teeth that extend outside the mouth of an animal such as walrus, elephant or wild boar.
tutu: A ballet skirt made of layered stiff but light netting.
tuxedo: A typically black formal jacket worn by men.
tweet: The sound of a bird; any short high-pitched sound or whistle.
tweezers: A small pincerlike instrument, usually made of metal, used for handling or picking up small objects (such as postage stamps), plucking out (plucking) hairs, pulling out slivers, etc.
twig: A small thin branch of a tree or bush.
twilight: The soft light in the sky seen before the rising and (especially) after the setting of the sun, occasioned by the illumination of the earth’s atmosphere by the direct rays of the sun and their reflection on the earth.
twins: Either of two people (or, less commonly, animals) who shared the same uterus at the same time; one who was born at the same birth as a sibling.
twitter: (sometimes proscribed) To tweet; to post an update to Twitter.
type: A grouping based on shared characteristics; a class.
typeface: The particular design of some type, font, or a font family.
typewriter: A device, at least partially mechanical, used to print text by pressing keys that cause type to be impressed through an inked ribbon onto paper.
typhoon: A weather phenomenon in the northwestern Pacific that is precisely equivalent to a hurricane, which results in wind speeds of 64 knots (118 km/h) or above. Equivalent to a cyclone in the Indian Ocean and Indonesia/Australia.
ultimatum: A final statement of terms or conditions made by one party to another, especially one that expresses a threat of reprisal or war.
umbrella: Cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
uncertainty: Doubt; the condition of being uncertain or without conviction.
uncle: The brother or brother-in-law of one’s parent.
underclothes: Clothes worn next to the skin and underneath outer clothing
underestimate: An estimate that is too low.
underground: An underground railway, especially for mass transit of people in urban areas.
underneath: The lower surface or part of something.
underpants: Underwear covering the genitalia and often buttocks, usually going no higher than the navel.
underpass: A passage that crosses a road, railroad or similar obstacle in a tunnel underneath it.
undershirt: An undergarment worn beneath a shirt, often collarless and sleeveless.
understanding: To grasp a concept fully and thoroughly, especially (of words, statements, art, etc.) to be aware of the meaning of and (of people) to be aware of the intent of.
undertaker: A funeral director; someone whose business is to manage funerals, burials and cremations.
underwear: Clothes worn next to the skin, underneath outer clothing.
underweight: The state or quality of being underweight.
underwire: A semicircular wire placed in a bra to support the breasts.
underwriting: To write below or under; subscribe.
unemployment: The state of having no job; joblessness.
unibody: An automobile construction technique in which the body is integrated into a single unit with the chassis rather than having a separate body-on-frame.
uniform: A distinctive outfit that serves to identify members of a group.
uniformity: The state of being uniform, alike and lacking variety.
union: The act of uniting or joining two or more things into one.
unique: A thing without a like; something unequalled or unparallelled.
unit: A particular, minute unit of mass, defined differently for different substances, but so that varying substances of the same general type have the property that one international unit of the one has the same effect on the human body as one international unit of the other.
unity: Oneness; the state or fact of being one undivided entity.
universe: Our universe, the sum of everything that exists in the cosmos, including time and space itself.
university: Institution of higher education (typically accepting students from the age of about 17 or 18, depending on country, but in some exceptional cases able to take younger students) where subjects are studied and researched in depth and degrees are offered.
update: An advisement providing more up-to-date information than currently known.
uplift: The act or result of being uplifted.
upper: A stimulant, such as amphetamine, that increases energy and decreases appetite.
urge: A strong desire; an itch to do something.
urgency: The quality or condition of being urgent
urn: A vase with a footed base.
usage: The manner or the amount of using; use.
user: One who uses or makes use of something, a consumer/client or an express or implied licensee (free user) or a trespasser.
usher: A person, in a church, cinema etc., who escorts people to their seats.
usual: The typical state of something, or something that is typical.
utensil: An instrument or device for domestic use, especially in the kitchen.
utility: The state or condition of being useful; usefulness.
vacation: Freedom from some business or activity.
vaccine: A substance given to stimulate the body's production of antibodies and provide immunity against a disease without causing the disease itself in the treatment, prepared from the agent that causes the disease (or a related, also effective, but safer disease), or a synthetic substitute.
vacuum: A region of space that contains no matter.
vagrant: A person who wanders from place to place; a nomad, a wanderer.
valance: A short curtain that usually hangs along the top edge of a window.
valentine: An expression of affection, especially romantic affection, usually in the form of greeting card, gift, or message given the object of one's affection, especially on February 14th.
validity: The state of being valid, authentic or genuine.
valley: An elongated depression between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.
valuable: A personal possession such as jewellery, of relatively great monetary value; — usually used in plural form.
value: The quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable.
vampire: A mythological undead creature said to feed on the blood of the living.
van: A covered vehicle used for carrying goods or people, usually roughly cuboid in shape, longer and higher than a car but smaller than a truck/lorry.
vanilla: Any tropical, climbing orchid of the genus Vanilla (especially Vanilla planifolia), bearing podlike fruit yielding an extract used in flavoring food or in perfumes.
vanity: That which is vain, futile, or worthless; that which is of no value, use or profit.
variability: The state or characteristic of being variable.
variant: Something that is slightly different from a type or norm.
variation: The act of varying; a partial change in the form, position, state, or qualities of a thing.
variety: The quality of being varied; diversity.
vascular: Relating to the flow of fluids, such as blood, lymph, or sap, through the body of an animal or plant, or to the vessels that carry such fluids
vase: An upright open container used mainly for displaying fresh, dried, or artificial flowers.
vault: An arched masonry structure supporting and forming a ceiling, whether freestanding or forming part of a larger building.
vaulting: To build as, or cover with a vault.
veal: The flesh of a calf (i.e. a young bovine) used for food.
vector: A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction; the signed difference between two points.
vegetarian: A person who does not eat animal flesh, or, in some cases, use any animal products.
vegetarianism: The practice of following a vegetarian diet.
vehicle: A conveyance; a device for carrying or transporting substances, objects or individuals.
veil: Something hung up or spread out to hide or protect the face, or hide an object from view; usually of gauze, crepe, or similar diaphanous material.
vein: A blood vessel that transports blood from the capillaries back to the heart.
veldt: The open pasture land or grassland of South Africa and neighboring countries.
vellum: A type of parchment paper made from the skin of a lamb, baby goat, or calf.
velocity: A vector quantity that denotes the rate of change of position with respect to time, or a speed with the directional component.
velodrome: An indoor arena, having an oval banked track for bicycle racing.
velvet: A closely woven fabric (originally of silk, now also of cotton or man-made fibres) with a thick short pile on one side.
vendor: A person or a company that vends or sells.
veneer: A thin decorative covering of fine material (usually wood) applied to coarser wood or other material.
vengeance: Revenge taken for an insult, injury, or other wrong.
venom: A poison carried by an animal, usually injected into an enemy or prey by biting or stinging.
venti: A cup of coffee larger than grande, usually 20 ounces.
venture: A risky or daring undertaking or journey.
venue: A theater, auditorium, arena, or other area designated for sporting or entertainment events.
veranda: A gallery, platform, or balcony, usually roofed and often partly enclosed, extending along the outside of a building.
verb: (grammar) A word that indicates an action, event, or state.
verdict: A decision on an issue of fact in a civil or criminal case or an inquest.
vermicelli: Long, slender pasta, similar to spaghetti, only thinner.
vernacular: The language of a people or a national language.
verse: A poetic form with regular meter and a fixed rhyme scheme.
version: A specific form or variation of something.
vertigo: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, caused by looking down from a great height or by disease affecting the inner ear.
verve: Excitement of imagination such as that which animates a poet, artist, or musician, in composing or performing
vessel: Any craft designed for transportation on water, such as a ship or boat.
vest: A loose robe or outer garment worn historically by men in Arab or Middle Eastern countries.
vestment: A robe, gown, or other article of clothing worn as an indication of office.
veteran: A person with long experience of a particular activity.
veterinarian: A medical doctor who treats animals.
veto: A political right to disapprove of (and thereby stop) the process of a decision, a law etc.
viability: The property of being viable; the ability to live or to succeed
vibraphone: A percussion instrument with a double row of tuned metal bars, each above the tubular resonator containing a motor-driven rotating vane, giving a vibrato effect.
vibration: The act of vibrating or the condition of being vibrated.
vibrissae: Any of the tactile whiskers on the nose of an animal such as a cat
vicinity: Proximity; the state of being near.
victim: One that is harmed—killed, injured, subjected to oppression, deceived, or otherwise adversely affected—by someone or something, especially another person or event, force, or condition; in particular:
victory: An instance of having won a competition or battle or succeeded in an effort.
viewer: Someone who views a spectacle; an onlooker or spectator.
vignette: A running ornament consisting of leaves and tendrils, used in Gothic architecture.
villa: (plural "villas") A house, often larger and more expensive than average, in the countryside or on the coast, often used as a retreat.
village: A rural habitation of size between a hamlet and a town.
vine: The climbing plant that produces grapes.
vinegar: A sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative; a dilute solution of acetic acid.
vineyard: A grape plantation, especially one used in the production of wine.
vintage: The yield of grapes or wine from a vineyard or district during one season.
vinyl: The univalent radical CH2=CH−, derived from ethylene.
viola: A stringed instrument of the violin family, somewhat larger than a violin, played under the chin, and having a deeper tone.
violation: The act or an instance of violating or the condition of being violated.
violet: A monocotyledonous plant (Allium cepa), allied to garlic, used as vegetable and spice.
violin: A musical four-string instrument, generally played with a bow or by plucking the string, with the pitch set by pressing the strings at the appropriate place with the fingers; also any instrument of the violin family.
virginal: A musical instrument in the harpsichord family.
virtue: Accordance with moral principles; conformity of behaviour or thought with the strictures of morality; good moral conduct.
virus: A submicroscopic, non-cellular structure consisting of a core of DNA or RNA surrounded by a protein coat, that requires a living host cell to replicate, and often causes disease in the host organism.
visa: A permit to enter and leave a country, normally issued by the authorities of the country to be visited.
viscose: A viscous orange-brown liquid obtained by chemical treatment of cellulose and used as the basis of manufacturing rayon and cellulose film.
vise: An instrument consisting of two jaws, closing by a screw, lever, cam, or the like, for holding work, as in filing.
vision: The sense or ability of sight.
visitor: Someone who visits someone else; someone staying as a guest.
visor: A part of a helmet, arranged so as to lift or open, and so show the face. The openings for seeing and breathing are generally in it.
vista: A distant view or prospect, especially one seen through some opening, avenue or passage.
visual: Any element of something that depends on sight.
vitality: The capacity to live and develop.
vitamin: Any of a specific group of organic compounds essential in small quantities for healthy human growth, metabolism, development, and body function; found in minute amounts in plant and animal foods or sometimes produced synthetically; deficiencies of specific vitamins produce specific disorders.
vodka: A clear distilled alcoholic liquor made from grain mash.
voice: Sound uttered by the mouth, especially by human beings in speech or song; sound thus uttered considered as possessing some special quality or character
volcano: A vent or fissure on the surface of a planet (usually in a mountainous form) with a magma chamber attached to the mantle of a planet or moon, periodically erupting forth lava and volcanic gases onto the surface.
volleyball: A game played on a rectangular court between two teams of two to six players which involves striking a ball back and forth over a net.
volume: A three-dimensional measure of space that comprises a length, a width and a height. It is measured in units of cubic centimeters in metric, cubic inches or cubic feet in English measurement.
volunteer: One who enters into, or offers for, any service of his/her own free will, especially when done without pay.
volunteering: To enlist oneself as a volunteer.
vomit: The regurgitated former contents of a stomach; vomitus.
vote: A formalized choice on matters of administration or other democratic activities
voting: To cast a vote; to assert a formalized choice in an election
voyage: A long journey, especially by ship.
vulture: Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae.
waffle: A flat pastry pressed with a grid pattern.
wage: (often in plural) An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
wagon: A four-wheeled cart for hauling loads.
waist: The part of the body between the pelvis and the stomach.
waistband: A band of fabric encircling the waist, especially a part of a pair of pants or a skirt.
waiter: A male or female attendant who serves customers at their tables in a restaurant, café or similar.
waiting: To delay movement or action until the arrival or occurrence of; to await. (Now generally superseded by “wait for”.)
waitress: A female attendant who serves customers in a restaurant, café, or similar.
waiver: The act of waiving, or not insisting on, some right, claim, or privilege.
wake: The act of waking, or state of being awake.
walk: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times. Compare run.
walker: The agent noun of to walk: a person who walks or a thing which walks, especially a pedestrian or a participant in a walking race.
walking: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times. Compare run.
walkway: A clearly defined path for pedestrians.
wall: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.
wallaby: Any of several species of marsupial; usually smaller and stockier than kangaroos
wallet: A small case, often flat and often made of leather, for keeping money (especially paper money), credit cards, etc.
walnut: A hardwood tree of the genus Juglans.
walrus: A large Arctic marine mammal related to seals and having long tusks, tough, wrinkled skin, and four flippers, Odobenus rosmarus.
wampum: Small beads made from polished shells, especially white ones, formerly used as money and jewelry by certain Native American peoples.
wannabe: Someone who wishes to be or do something, but lacks the qualifications or talent; an overeager amateur; an aspirant.
war: Organized, large-scale, armed conflict between countries or between national, ethnic, or other sizeable groups, usually involving the engagement of military forces.
wardrobe: A room for keeping clothes and armor safe, particularly a dressing room or walk-in closet beside a bedroom.
warfare: The waging of war or armed conflict against an enemy.
warlock: A male magic-user; a male witch.
warlord: A high military officer in a warlike nation.
warm-up: The act of exercising or stretching in preparation for strenuous activity
warmth: A moderate degree of heat; the sensation of being warm.
warning: To make (someone) aware of (something impending); especially:
warrant: Authorization or certification; a sanction, as given by a superior.
warren: The system of burrows where rabbits live.
warrior: A person who is actively engaged in battle, conflict or warfare; a soldier or combatant.
wasabi: A pungent green Japanese condiment made from the plant Eutrema japonicum (formerly Wasabia japonica).
wash: The process or an instance of washing or being washed by water or other liquid.
washbasin: A basin used for washing, particularly a permanently installed sink, fitted with a water supply and a drain, for washing the hands and face.
washcloth: A small cloth used to wash the face and body.
washer: Something that washes; especially an appliance such as a washing machine or dishwasher.
washtub: A tub used for washing clothes.
wasp: Any of many types of stinging flying insect resembling a hornet.
waste: Excess of material, useless by-products or damaged, unsaleable products; garbage; rubbish.
wastebasket: A usually small indoor receptacle for items that are to be discarded; a rubbish bin.
watchmaker: A person who repairs (and originally made) watches.
water: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.
waterbed: A bed with a tough plastic mattress filled with water.
watercress: A perennial European herb, Nasturtium officinale, that grows in freshwater streams; used in salads and as a garnish.
waterfall: A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
waterfront: The land alongside a body of water.
watermelon: A plant of the species Citrullus lanatus, bearing a melon-like fruit.
waterskiing: The sport of riding on water skis, whilst being towed by a motorboat.
waterspout: A whirlwind that forms over water, not associated with a mesocyclone of a thunderstorm (contrary to a true tornado).
waterwheel: A wheel, propelled by running or falling water, used to power machinery.
wave: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
waveform: The shape of a wave function represented by a graph showing some dependent variable as function of an independent variable.
way: (heading) To do with a place or places.
weapon: An instrument of attack or defense in combat or hunting, e.g. most guns, missiles, or swords.
weather: The short term state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including the temperature, relative humidity, cloud cover, precipitation, wind, etc.
webinar: An interactive seminar conducted via Internet. Usually a live presentation, lecture or workshop that happens in real time, as users participate through text-based chat, voice, video, or file-sharing.
webmail: A service for sending, receiving, and/or storing email, usually on a remote web server, in such a way that it is accessible through a web browser.
webpage: A single hypertext document (transmitted as HTML) on the World Wide Web, often hyperlinked to others, and intended to be viewed with a web browser.
website: A collection of interlinked web pages on the World Wide Web that are typically accessible from the same base URL and reside on the same server.
wedding: To perform the marriage ceremony for; to join in matrimony.
wedge: One of the simple machines; a piece of material, such as metal or wood, thick at one edge and tapered to a thin edge at the other for insertion in a narrow crevice, used for splitting, tightening, securing, or levering.
weed: Any plant regarded as unwanted at the place where, and at the time when it is growing.
weedkiller: A chemical agent that destroys unwanted plants (weeds) but not wanted ones (crops etc)
week: Any period of seven consecutive days.
weekend: The break in the working week, usually two days including the traditional holy or sabbath day. Thus in western countries, Saturday and Sunday.
weekender: Someone who visits a place for a weekend break.
welcome: The act of greeting someone’s arrival, especially by saying "Welcome!"; reception.
welfare: Health, safety, happiness and prosperity; well-being in any respect.
well-being: A state of health, happiness and/or prosperity.
west: One of the four principal compass points, specifically 270°, conventionally directed to the left on maps; the direction of the setting sun at an equinox, abbreviated as W.
western: A film, or some other dramatic work, set in, the historic (c. 1850-1910) American West (west of the Mississippi river) focusing on conflict between whites and Indians, lawmen and outlaws, ranchers and farmers, or industry (railroads, mining) and agriculture.
wetland: (usually in the plural) Land that is covered mostly with water, with occasional marshy and soggy areas.
wetsuit: A close fitting, insulating garment usually made from neoprene or similar material designed to keep one warm during activities on or under water.
whale: Any of several species of large sea mammals of the infraorder Cetacea.
wharf: A man-made landing place for ships on a shore or river bank.
wheat: Any of several cereal grains, of the genus Triticum, that yields flour as used in bakery.
wheel: A circular device capable of rotating on its axis, facilitating movement or transportation or performing labour in machines.
whelp: A young offspring of a canid (ursid, felid, pinniped), especially of a dog or a wolf, the young of a bear or similar mammal (lion, tiger, seal); a pup, wolf cub.
whey: The liquid remaining after milk has been curdled and strained in the process of making cheese.
whip: A lash; a pliant, flexible instrument, such as a rod (commonly of cane or rattan) or a plaited or braided rope or thong (commonly of leather) used to create a sharp "crack" sound for directing or herding animals.
whirlwind: A violent windstorm of limited extent, as the tornado, characterized by an inward spiral motion of the air with an upward current in the center; a vortex of air. It usually has a rapid progressive motion.
whisker: That part of the beard which grows upon the sides of the face, usually of the male, or upon the chin, or upon both.
whiskey: A liquor distilled from the fermented mash of grain (as rye, corn, or barley).
whisper: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially, without vibration of the vocal cords.
whistle: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.
white: The color/colour of snow or milk; the colour of light containing equal amounts of all visible wavelengths.
whole: Something complete, without any parts missing.
wholesale: The sale of products, often in large quantities, to retailers or other merchants.
wholesaler: A person or company that buys merchandise from manufacturers, importers, or distributors and resells the merchandise to retail businesses and to business and institutional end users.
wick: A bundle, twist, braid, or woven strip of cord, fabric, fibre/fiber, or other porous material in a candle, oil lamp, kerosene heater, or the like, that draws up liquid fuel, such as melted tallow, wax, or the oil, delivering it to the base of the flame for conversion to gases and burning; any other length of material burned for illumination in small successive portions.
widget: A placeholder name for an unnamed, unspecified, or hypothetical manufactured good or product.
widow: A woman whose spouse has died (and who has not remarried); feminine of widower.
wife: A married woman, especially in relation to her spouse.
wifi: Any of several standards for short-range wireless data transmission (IEEE 802.11).
wild: The undomesticated state of a wild animal
wilderness: An unsettled and uncultivated tract of land in its natural state; a barren land; a wild or waste.
wildlife: Animals, plants, and fungi, not normally domesticated, often to the exclusion of plants, fungi, fish, insects and other invertebrates, and microscopic plants and animals; hence:
will: (now uncommon or literary) To wish, desire (something).
willow: Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix, in the willow family Salicaceae, found primarily on moist soils in cooler zones in the northern hemisphere.
wind: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.
windage: Drag on the crankshaft caused by oil splashing out of the sump when rotating at high speeds.
window: The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant.
windscreen: A transparent screen made of glass, located at the front of a vehicle in order to protect its occupants from the wind and weather
windshield: A transparent screen made of glass, located at the front and back of a vehicle in front of its occupants to protect them from the wind and weather.
wine: An alcoholic beverage made by fermenting the juice of grapes.
winery: A place where wine is made, or a company that makes wine.
wing: An appendage of an animal's (bird, bat, insect) body that enables it to fly; a similar fin at the side of a ray or similar fish
wingman: A pilot partner of another, a pilot who flies in the same wing or squadron.
wingtip: The extreme tip of the wing of an aircraft, bird, flying insect, etc.
wink: An act of winking (a blinking of only one eye), or a message sent by winking.
winner: One who has won or often wins.
winter: Traditionally the fourth of the four seasons, typically regarded as being from December 23 to March 20 in continental regions of the Northern Hemisphere or the months of June, July and August in the Southern Hemisphere. It is the time when the sun is lowest in the sky, resulting in short days, and the time of year with the lowest atmospheric temperatures for the region.
wire: Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.
wiretap: A connection installed on a telephone line or other communications system in order to allow a third party to conduct covert surveillance of conversations.
wiring: To fasten with wire, especially with reference to wine bottles, corks, or fencing.
wisdom: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.
wiseguy: One who is insolent or flippant; one who makes jokes or perpetrates pranks.
wish: A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen.
wisteria: Any of several woody climbing vines, of the genus Wisteria, native to the East Asian countries of China, Korea, and Japan and the eastern United States.
witch: A person who practices witchcraft; a woman or man who practices witchcraft.
witch-hunt: A search for people believed to be using sorcery or harmful magic, especially in order to punish them.
withdrawal: Receiving from someone's care what one has earlier entrusted to them. Usually refers to money.
witness: Attestation of a fact or event; testimony.
wok: A large, oriental, round-bottomed cooking pan.
wolf: The gray wolf, specifically all subspecies of the gray wolf (Canis lupus) that are not dingoes or dogs.
wombat: Any of several herbivorous, burrowing marsupials, of the family Vombatidae, mainly found in southern and eastern Australia.
wonder: Something that causes amazement or awe; a marvel.
wont: One's habitual way of doing things; custom, habit, practice.
wood: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
woodchuck: A rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots, Marmota monax.
woodshed: An enclosed, roofed structure, often an outbuilding, used primarily to store firewood.
woodwind: Any (typically wooden) musical instrument that produces sound by the player blowing into it, through a reed, or across an opening. Woodwind instruments include the recorder, flute, piccolo, clarinet, oboe, cor anglais and bassoon.
wool: The hair of the sheep, llama and some other ruminants.
word: The smallest unit of language that has a particular meaning and can be expressed by itself; the smallest discrete, meaningful unit of language. (contrast morpheme.)
wording: To say or write (something) using particular words; to phrase (something).
workbench: A sturdy bench or table at which manual work is done by a carpenter, machinist, etc.
worker: A person who performs labor for a living, especially manual labor.
workforce: All the workers employed by a specific organization or state, or on a specific project
workhorse: A horse used primarily for manual labor; a draft horse
workout: An exercise session; a period of physical exercise.
workshop: A room, especially one which is not particularly large, used for manufacturing or other light industrial work.
world: (with "the") Human collective existence; existence in general.
worm: A generally tubular invertebrate of the annelid phylum; an earthworm.
worship: The condition of being worthy; honour, distinction.
worshiper: A person who worships, especially at a place of assembly for religious services.
wound: An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.
wrap: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
wraparound: A garment that is wrapped around the body and tied.
wrapper: Something that is wrapped around something else as a cover or protection: a wrapping.
wrapping: The material in which something is wrapped.
wreck: Something or someone that has been ruined.
wrecker: A person or company that dismantles old or wrecked vehicles or other items, to reclaim useful parts. (Australia)
wren: Any member of a mainly New World passerine bird family Troglodytidae; true wren.
wrench: A movement that twists or pulls violently; a tug.
wrinkle: A small furrow, ridge or crease in an otherwise smooth surface.
wrist: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
writer: A person who writes, or produces literary work.
writing: Graphism of symbols such as letters that express some meaning.
wrong: Something that is immoral or not good.
xylophone: Any musical instrument (percussion idiophone) made of wooden slats graduated so as to make the sounds of the scale when struck with a small drumstick-like mallet; the standard Western concert xylophone or one of its derivatives.
yacht: A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence offshore on a dock.
yahoo: A rough, coarse, loud or uncouth person; yokel; lout.
yak: An ox-like mammal native to the Himalayas, Mongolia, Burma, and Tibet with dark, long, and silky hair, a horse-like tail, and a full, bushy mane.
yam: Any climbing vine of the genus Dioscorea in the Eastern and Western hemispheres, usually cultivated.
yang: A principle in Chinese and related East Asian philosophies associated with bright, hot, masculine, etc. elements of the natural world.
yard: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
yarmulke: A skullcap worn by religious Jewish males (especially during prayer).
yarn: A twisted strand of fiber used for knitting or weaving.
yawl: A small ship's boat, usually rowed by four or six oars.
year: A solar year, the time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
yeast: An often humid, yellowish froth produced by fermenting malt worts, and used to brew beer, leaven bread, and also used in certain medicines.
yellow: The colour of gold, butter, or a lemon; the colour obtained by mixing green and red light, or by subtracting blue from white light.
yellowjacket: A predatory wasp with alternating black and yellow stripes around the abdomen, usually of the genera Vespula or Dolichovespula.
yesterday: The day immediately before today; one day ago.
yew: A species of coniferous tree, Taxus baccata, with dark-green flat needle-like leaves and seeds bearing red arils, native to western, central and southern Europe, northwest Africa, northern Iran and southwest Asia.
yin: A principle in Chinese and related East Asian philosophies associated with dark, cool, female, etc. elements of the natural world.
yoga: Any of several Hindu or Buddhist disciplines aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquillity; especially a system of exercises practiced to promote control of the body and mind.
yogurt: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
yoke: Frame around the neck, and related senses.
yolk: The yellow, spherical part of an egg that is surrounded by the white albumen, and serves as nutriment for the growing young.
young: People who are young; young people, collectively; youth.
youth: The quality or state of being young.
yoyo: A toy consisting of a spheroidal or cylindrical spindle having a circular groove in which string is wound; it is used by holding the string in the fingers and reeling the spindle up and down by movements of the wrist.
yurt: A large, round, semi-permanent tent with vertical walls and a conical roof, usually associated with Central Asia and Mongolia (where it is known as a ger).
zebra: Any of three species of genus Equus: E. grevyi, E. quagga, or E. zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa.
zephyr: A light wind from the west.
zero: The numeric symbol that represents the cardinal number zero.
ziggurat: A temple tower of the ancient Mesopotamian valley, having the form of a terraced pyramid of successively receding stories
zinc: A chemical element (symbol Zn) with an atomic number of 30, a slightly brittle blue-silvery metal.
zither: A musical instrument consisting of a flat sounding box with numerous strings placed on a horizontal surface, played with a plectrum or fingertips.
zombie: A snake god or fetish in religions of West Africa and elsewhere.
zone: Each of the five regions of the earth's surface into which it was divided by climatic differences, namely the torrid zone (between the tropics), two temperate zones (between the tropics and the polar circles), and two frigid zones (within the polar circles).
zoo: A park where live animals are exhibited.
zoology: The part of biology relating to the animal kingdom, including the structure, embryology, evolution, classification, habits, and distribution of all animals, both living and extinct.
zucchini: A courgette; a variety of squash, Cucurbita pepo, which bears edible fruit.
